Inside Elections just moved our race from "Tilt Democratic" to "Toss-up."
That means one thing: This race is going to be one of the closest House races in the entire country.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email?]

National Republicans have had their eye on this seat for years because they think it's one of their best opportunities to flip a district that will determine who controls Congress.
And now, one of the top election analysts in the country is confirming what we've known all along: This race will come down to the wire.
The truth is, I've never taken anything for granted. Not in 2022. Not in 2024. And certainly not now.
We won’t win automatically — not in a district this competitive. And to be honest, I wouldn’t want to. I work every day to earn this district’s votes because that’s exactly how democracy should work.
But now, we’re facing a flood of outside money that's about to pour into Southwest Washington because control of the House could come down to just a handful of seats.

Peter,

America turns 250 this July 4th.

I grew up all over Montana. Miles City. Helena. Dillon. Victor. Great Falls. July 4th looked a little different in each town but it always felt the same. We were proud. Not because someone told us to be. Just because we were.

My dad taught high school math. My mom taught elementary school. They were public servants their whole lives and they raised me to believe this country was worth showing up for.

_I still believe that._

I spent years as Montana's U.S. Attorney going after the cartels and criminals threatening families and communities. Now I am running for Senate because I think the next 250 years of this country are worth fighting for just as hard as the last.

Before July 4th, I want to ask you something. What does America mean to you?

name: Kurt Alme
subject: 250 years of American greatness
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alme for Senate
body:
This July 4th is unlike any other. I want to hear from you. |
---
Fellow Patriot,

America turns 250 this July 4th.

I grew up all over Montana. Miles City. Helena. Dillon. Victor. Great Falls. July 4th looked a little different in each town but it always felt the same. We were proud. Not because someone told us to be. Just because we were.

My dad taught high school math. My mom taught elementary school. They were public servants their whole lives and they raised me to believe this country was worth showing up for.

_I still believe that._

I spent years as Montana's U.S. Attorney going after the cartels and criminals threatening families and communities. Now I am running for Senate because I think the next 250 years of this country are worth fighting for just as hard as the last.

Before July 4th, I want to ask you something. What does America mean to you?

clean_body: This July 4th is unlike any other. I want to hear from you. | Fellow Patriot, America turns 250 this July 4th. I grew up all over Montana. Miles City. Helena. Dillon. Victor. Great Falls. July 4th looked a little different in each town but it always felt the same. We were proud. Not because someone told us to be. Just because we were. My dad taught high school math. I spent years as Montana's U.S. Attorney going after the cartels and criminals threatening families and communities. | I’m writing to ask for $3 to help me stop Republicans from putting a 2020 election denier in Georgia's governor's mansion -- where he could refuse to certify any Democratic win in the state.

No, that’s not a typo.

**Georgia’s Lieutenant Governor Burt Jones was one of the 16 fake electors who signed a false certificate claiming Donald Trump won Georgia in 2020. A certificate that was sent to Congress to try to block the certification of Joe Biden’s win.**

Now he wants to be Governor of Georgia, where he would be responsible for certifying our state's 2028 presidential election results.

I’m Keisha Lance Bottoms, the Democrat running to stop him.

We've won our primary election. I am officially the Democratic nominee for Governor of Georgia, and I need your help. [](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/112293?t=6&akid=25088%2E878179%2E98wUgF) I know $3 might not seem like a lot – and that’s because it’s not.

But combined with thousands of other grassroots donors chipping in, your $3 has an enormous impact.

$3 helps us travel across the state, invest in critical resources, and fight back against the millions that Rick Jackson and Burt Jones are spending to lie about my record.

And $3 helps us fight back against Donald Trump’s attempts to steal this state by suppressing the vote.

Donald Trump took to Truth Social to push Congress to pass the "Save America" Act--the most heinous voting restrictions in the history of the country.
It has already failed to pass in the Senate, with some vulnerable MAGA Senators worried the bill would be so extreme that the backlash would cause them to lose their seats to Democrats.

And how does the Pentagon's top brass feel about it? This was Pete Hegseth's response to Trump on social media:
---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001shdB-_YWRiU9LGTT-U72XSfmWdXzA1Vr07xItLNvkbKfczlXT-nUuuJlbQeAurk64FRkdeCudB25-Zj0_yJi3e-lGs73UHwNb0oToEbU6UKKyCadvDlaAbUSmY8rGe6XMYW4COpqIXqJQLh44H5dtN2Wn_QQvIFxJSWKsycz_1Wk4EUkSzF6r2H6LBKoV9OazIuReCJh6gPhvldPhudJisawYCyt3h8FAnSLYJ9350c=&c=4-GgZOqMIFeq5Z147aLad93xojMAtWNAupyEghXoHu6MWDqAVqwrEQ==&ch=Rc8PHMD9yUyV-CaQb7yLj-ACFeJTHhN75THEQaeax0hGVAUjR2Z98g==)

Since the founding of this nation, the military has separated itself from partisan politics. It's a key tenet of the separation of powers and there are multiple laws and military directives preventing personnel from being used for political purposes. But Trump and Hegseth not only seemed prepared but intending to cross that rubicon.
Trump's assault on free and fair elections escalates every single day. While we don't know what the full picture of his plans for November look like, the pieces are coming together and it's not pretty. The gears are motion and he has the sycophants and crooks by his side ready and willing to do anything and everything necessary to make sure MAGA wins.
We have to rapidly build a firewall to protect our democracy from Trump. That's why Defend Our Courts exists. We successfully defended the pro-democracy majority on the Pennsylvania and Wisconsin Supreme Court over the past year--safeguarding election integrity in critical swing states.
Now we're expanding the scope of our mission to meet the gravity of the threats our democracy faces at this moment: Building a firewall of state Supreme Courts with the power to protect free and fair elections state by state. And leading the movement to reform the MAGA occupied U.S. Supreme Court that is enabling Trump's dismantling of our democracy.

This court has been fully exposed as a puppet of Trump and MAGA extremists, willing to torch a half-century of precedent to tilt elections their way.

## Trump Cancels Iran Strikes, Touts Deal
President Trump [canceled planned strikes](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFypDAQBNCvgUxbYha0KFBwCZkvvZCalQaYs5AoaWzM31-t7xMcd1VXv_7zNr8hR07rb9zJyZLnRGeNJEJllvKxHx6Tp1hRBP17rQd6-ppBg1HaqA7mgByvuW-DW4iA7i257jF2MIyjfbSbM36k3gQcjQ1oQdsebW_1HeCpn3oYWnavNm066LQeu-EGi316A8aPth-WwTe9psCSy-1v5iQbLfHKn1RuPu9tdJvIUZv7rwamBqbzPG9L_nopXnkD05EjC_vawPQNUhWvqjaq6j-NguKCSVUp_E5VYQhVHVkoCWNUgTCqymvitCrJClPKH8lTUHXLReLVFheOk2Pkah5Nr9cdOX5vkx8d-ungXwAAAP__i46OHg) against Iran on Thursday, saying treaty negotiations have been approved at "the highest level of Iranian leadership," with a signing to be announced shortly. The reversal came hours after Trump threatened to [seize Kharg Island](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1u8yAUxvGrgc0RHAPGA8O7eMu7drQIHGIa_CE4TZq7rxL1Djo_0l_6PR_n-exzydv1v1_RUdrnDR-tIBHWmerXegS_BSzNE_lwa-3wAb9nEGA6YToJc_S5PGfFo0uIgD1HJwcrQVs7DnxxPVo7qIsJw8WKGFEb0RtANHKUSanIs3vVhJEghbBSnyCNl2DABDsqnXRgSmDMtNfT5543WjCV537Hegr7yotbiI7G-n8MJgYTLbjkUl4bg-nYSw5PBlPEhFtDBpMeQfRWd29c96vrcvVb16jmGzYGE68uHo9cSm5mYEpcV5_fTU5_Ounu4CcAAP__YGR7IA), the hub of Iran's oil exports, and take control of the country's energy industry. Trump said a deal could be signed within days and that the terms had been approved by all parties, including Israel, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Egypt. Iran hasn't publicly confirmed an agreement. [See Trump's post](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0M2OozAQBOCngVsiuwH_HHxYacUte1ppj6ixm-Adg5HdSSZvP2JeYa5V0idV_btNN4wp7vc_uJHjJU87vWoiZioTl8d2eNw9pYrM6D9qPdDT5wQC1EWoi4QpYEzvqW-DW4iAupac1EbCYIzV7epmOwOgEaQNmGAgmBk9dkqrWWmruza6UxNKghTCyOEKi529AuWN7Ydl8E0vKETO5fo_x51XWtI7P6lcfd7a5FbmozbdrwbGBkYuD15r9hHT2Z9hLwph-p13TOHvOamB8ciVawOjlEp3oAawVksQUvVtceF4xZRiVbrpxX3D-E21_KN_ng6-AgAA__9hGnd3). The announcement came in the wake of an exchange of attacks by both nations, including an Iranian drone downing a U.S. Army helicopter near the Strait of Hormuz. The crew was rescued safely. [Watch the announcement of last night's canceled attack here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuwyAYBOCnwRsW_DbYHhi6eEvXjtZv-J3QYLCAxs3bV8krdD7pdN99XZYL-uDj9RN3MnVLS6SzBKqV8lLzz35YjJZCwVrR3ks50NLvAgI0F5pLWBz68Fz6xpmNCKhryMhhlKDGcRqam9G9Vh0JWNex6wZHq7IwuHXQdhrlIEXjzatNaAlSiFGqFrZptRq0HadebcqyXpDzNeX2O_lYb7SFZ3pQbm3am2ButR6FdR8MZgbzeZ5tXO1L8coZzDGdDOaHd5QYzG8TtxhC4Wnb-BEwRnK81OzvVHiK3GeMHHfv-JHTNVMpvKYTsyscuSMMHHQ_KdVrqTvVZOOO04fgix5YL647-vCeVv_158PAXwAAAP__rRGKjQ).
## White House Taps Jay Clayton as New Intel Chief
President Trump said Thursday he will [nominate Jay Clayton](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OqzAQhZ_GdCB7-IkpXNyGLrfdEg1mCM4ONoJJWN5-RV5hm9Mc6Ts639e9v2PgEB__cSEnU-ojHTuTCG29bK9l9Rg98Y4i6L_3fUVPPz1oaHLd5Ab6EQOffZWNbiICKjNy5mYN1Na2t2x27QAlDmBNjQYGbakqB6p9RQO2WNk6C-6i6caA0dqauoCpHXwDjbdtVU-1V5WmMUjaimcKUWaa-Exv2gqflozdLLLuqvynoFPQHcdR-Dj4q1TQXWgFnb7CGAXd51P-xDP3jKekmEeUkCJyHqIQc3hQ9JSvLxYqZlk429y4HoE57M1NVfqxYODPtvxJ2NvBbwAAAP__LE5_lA), Manhattan's top federal prosecutor and former chairman of the Securities and Exchange Commission, as the next director of national intelligence. Trump wrote on social media that few people in the legal community "are respected at the level of Jay" and urged the Senate to confirm him quickly. [See the post](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0M1q6zAUBOCnsXcJ0rF-F1pcuHiXrgpdGkU6jtXKlpFOkubti_sK3c7ABzMfl-niU07b7c2v6Ggu04bPlpEI60T1vu7BbwFz80Q-fLW2-4DfEzBQJ6ZOHKboU35Noo9uRgQcenRcGw7SGKv7xRkfwhWEFWweohKDDFKiiRqDssiuvk_u0JjiwBkzXJ5httegQAVjhZxl6ATDmKjU82dJGy0451d5YD2HsvbZLUR764Z_HYwdjFTvtLQSks9Hf4SCVfT5f9l8ju_HpA7GvTRqHYycKz2A1tpYY43UxvbVxf2Zck5N6U6w2-rTL9XTn_55OPgJAAD__-3HeCU). The nomination follows congressional pushback over Trump's choice of housing regulator Bill Pulte, who has [no intelligence background](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1uhDAQhJ_GdEZm-S9cpKG7tCnRYtZ3vhgb2ZsjvH3EvUK6kUaa0fd93eYbOu_C_RM30mzjHOjInpgpzZx-tt1gMOQzMqP5znlHQ78zKOik6mQF84rOn3NTrNoSAdUF6aofKmiHYeyLh15Haxeol8ZUS9c3yzisdsSBLNUKVd0WTl9rqqugUmqo2hLsuJgOOjOMTWtbIxpFq-OYymd0gR9k_RlflEoTt8LrB_OeRf0hYBIwHcdRmiVfFFcvYLqigOmJpzQeT45BvsHk6hIZjklGKwOyiwG9dIHJe3enYEjAVCS97ofz3uWuF426b-j8-5j_Zeul4S8AAP__rZKBRw), to serve as acting director starting June 19. Hours earlier, Congress rejected a short-term extension of a [key surveillance law](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFygzAQRL9GdHjEATIqVKShc9qUzCEd5hwhMXCxw99nzC-kfju78_brNtyQI6f7Jy7kZMpDotceSYS2QbafZfWYPMUdRdB_7_uKnn4H0GBKbcoKhoAcj6EpgpuIgOqCXHXtKmi7zl6L2XUjWUQINlS2bq0Z7RgmCr6e7NhhqAt27zZtKqi07qr2ApMdvQHjO9u0U-tVoymw5O3yyJxkpike-UnbxeeliG4WWXdVfyjoFfQy08wxvpmCfs4LvYUU9BgWTrzLhsI5KehbC7qpTXlaljkkLlNeOJ28fOBR-oiHnNlic2F9cYy8m6tq9H1BPjcK-ddpTwd_AQAA__8AGILu) after Democrats objected to the Pulte pick. Section 702, which allows warrantless monitoring of foreigners abroad, expires today.
## SpaceX IPO Mints Employee Millionaires
SpaceX begins trading on the Nasdaq today in what's expected to be the [largest IPO in history](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1yhCAUhZ9GO3bgiggFRRq7TZvSYeGykqA4crPuvn3G5BFSnzPn5_u4TleXclrv725BS7FMKx41IxHuE-3fy-bd6jFXR-T8V62b8_icgINiXDEBU3ApvybZBhsRAbsWrRi0gF5rM7SzNU4MUUKUOnh05mZCh0p7ENy4IIeuTfZM40qA4FyL_gLR3LwC5bWRfex9IzmGRGW_fJa00owxv8oD94svS5vtTLTVpntrYGxgpBlXfNKBt1NuYDz_NDD-DWdpK0xyztmSck5ldWnHynDZcnkhVnagyzS3uw3bcTqqGhrJ74tL-beO_sXoYeEnAAD__w5QfNg), a $1.75 trillion debut set to make millionaires out of more than 4,000 current and former employees. The windfall reaches well beyond the engineering labs. Stock went to [workers at every level](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2S2zAMhuHTSB09ItaU6IJFGnebNqUGAsE1Y_5oSHgV3z7j-Ajpn8Hg_X59rp8YUyxfPzGzk1DXwkdPLMJtlfbIO2EhTh1FkO6970j8Z4UJZjXNSsPqMabneh69C8zAHyM7vVgNxtrLMt6cJ7-RQU0aL4BhMdsEft5mpM2YjXCM7nVtmjXoabLanCBcNpphJns5m2BoOE_so9R2-l1jkRuH9Kzf3E5U85jcTWTvw8ePAa4DXI_jOGVsd5ZOjbm82QDXV9cA13eA6lLprt5QhVQFJdaiqD6SVxnvrORWHx2L76oGxXlP9cncVY4pxVowNu6KeAmGvPXWUtCwjM35_XiJPi_DefrKGNO_N-W_tv128DcAAP__pNqS_A), including the welders, machinists, and cafeteria cooks who built the rocket program. One former welder who joined the company in 2015, [making $28 an hour,](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkc2umzAQhZ_G7CbCBgwsWKSq2N2qUhddIsc-BPf6B9lOuHn7ivQRuj3zaWa-md8fy4eyzob7D-UxlTUuAUd2KAVpKenhd62ChsuqFKU_c96VxtciaiGplsTFYpR1r6WtzLQCAk2FifcDF90wjH21TVqutbwNvRk475rRaN5yLVdueNPLFrqy09mtllzwuh54dxHreNNSSD2Mbbd2mrU1jC0xXf5EG8qG1b3iE-mio6_ctJWyZ9ZcmZiZmI_juPgczhoTMwI9MhOzjwEvJuY7ApJyZwIUKhvonxHB7y6-gEzHFkklUD6BSDfo6EH-4Yr11jkbg7IJmcqmwmc-EVsy2T3SmqInfEG_UzwR6IAzSOcKKtH1Krr4cxtZM0dtDWu-fzsvjyP_QtqrNJn9OCdk2bO2vntl3dux_NdjnpP4GwAA__8VE6Y4) is sitting on shares worth roughly $880,000. Shares held by some employees could be worth tens of millions of dollars or more. Real estate agents near company hubs are already fielding calls about everything from [lakefront condos](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDFytTAQg09jOhh7AQOFi7-he3-bklmbNTgxhsGbR97tMyRHSKNGmk8jvT2mB4YY0vIfNzLs9ynRlSMx0znx-bkdDpOjmJEZ3UfOBzr6mkCCLqUuFUwzhviammI2ngioLsiorlfQ9v3QFatpPFitUJNHr3XT1jXVtlOz7Qcga4cimJsmtQIlZa_aCvxgnQbt-qFpfetEI2kOvJ_V-x4Sr-Tja3_SWbl9K6JZmY8s6n8CRgHjdV2VS9bdpoDxRgsY5S1KCRh_B5RbiDHsCcNJubwII69lPijNIS3VylssTjMf153KuhONXDYM8aeR_3TT08B3AAAA__9ySXv9) to 1,000-acre ranches. Brown Convention Center, under a historically unified spirit. Gov. Greg Abbott emerged as a top sponsor, while Texas House Speaker Dustin Burrows becomes the [first sitting speaker](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkbGO3CAURb8Gd4zg2QZcuEjjbtOmtJ7h4SHDgAXseP330awU5QNS3eJIRzq6vz7WDwwxpP0nPmluXz6vic4aqTUq654Pm9OLUgs5HVQf10Fos32sIEBxobiE1WGI1zp0bt6Em2RHs9RGggKAvrvPKI03RnrtaZSiJ7TKGbPZydNI46i6ML9lQkmQUvSDuA0SrTZ6c7o3XmrJBkEutFxu7U6NvrD6eOUXlZvNzy7O99aOyvofDBYGy3metwelOr4pgwVLCzYSg-UdxmCJ2WJksHyb_i4vdHxuMVhMleeDEq8NG_F_-fwo-TfZFtLOP1NoF0ffqPCLsFSePQ_Jh_3-5gwW0D03bjKIW8-1JMMHZQWfRj3xwYAyw6hcT0NXZnecIcZQlWaD2J8Y4ndX-783XjP8CQAA__-Ts59i) to address the gathering, signaling reconciliation between elected officials and grassroots activists. Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, Abbott, Burrows, and Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick are [scheduled to speak today](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHSqyAQhZ8GOxx2NZAUFLexy21v6QASZULAgTXGt78Tm_8B_marb_ac7_y7j3cTYkjzX_Pymj6PPCa_1-iJfBnnvLqc3j5RyGn19Xms3rjsniMKlFxIDjhOJsRj7JtJWzHdoPEa1BVQImLXLNoYb-FiL9aBUxJ72VtpXaekRYVwc03Q32dCAgKIrhdtD8apq7KT6q4PUMB64adAubS0ePIfUx_xyG9fWpdfTdQL0VpZ94fhwHDY9709ISrBbsm3ucwMh28Gw0F8DwDD4WT4nFf-o8hPrSVvlXLixtpMxO1WSt4r31Kgg-HQFD2te4gxVKlYL-aXCfGsQr8b8K3xfwAAAP__pXiFLQ), urging Republicans to unify as a party ahead of challenging November midterms. ## Couple Sentenced to 40 Years for Pyramid Scheme
A Frisco couple was [sentenced to 40 years each in federal prison](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2S4yAUhE-DMlTwYEEbEGyizJtOqMLwZFHmrwRjWbefkq8wWQdfd3X312252RBDfvy3CU1_r2XJeLSIveO-PEp1Jb8w91ByxfY8K1pX3HMBBooyRTks3oZ4LnLw5s78Xz6g4XrioABADJtRdz2BUk4rUH-scEppOyED5EJIC2II5gpjigPnTEg2Sm6dnvTdazGtXHMiGfrQyz72DTu-bVvjWV64j66kIZqt99qI-EdgJjAfxzGu5S2vGRdAYL4kgfljpa5814i0Ye6YHXoqGT3R7o0KRlOIMZRMq80eU3C0nrtNwdPmNkw47MbX42Ka0kSyR7Ihflr03333MvATAAD__1CqhLE) for running a $30 million illegal pyramid scheme that defrauded more than 10,000 people nationwide during the COVID-19 pandemic. LaShonda Moore, 38, and Marlon Moore, 39, were convicted by a jury in January on conspiracy, wire fraud, and money laundering charges, the [Justice Department said](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDFuwyAUQE-DNyz4UOwMDF28pWtHi8CPTYMBAbHj21fNFXqA9570vq_z1fjg4_JlNtTtdU9zxKMGbA3LvKRsU9wxNp9ixvo4Mxqb7GMGBooyRTnMzvhwzrJz-sbchXeo-TByUAAgulVbvDC8IBp-AztKJSx-2BFAMikUF67z-k_GFAfOmZCsl9zYYRxubhDjnQ-cSIbOt1T6tmLDl6n3cKYdS2_T1gW9tpYrEZ8EJgLTcRz9z7M2b7Ff0k5gStkQmHIhML1patMzB6QVY8No0dHyjNHHhfoQcDGB5rOYzTta7YobdkW7fPgQfFUDkWzZjA_vdvvfsV3DbwAAAP__R6mCZw). Their "Blessings in No Time" program operated from June 2020 to June 2021. name: The PreBorn! Team
subject: The abortion pill was already in her cart
body:
The abortion pill was already sitting in her online cart when she found PreBorn!.

| | | | [](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckcGq3SAQhp_G7E7QMTHJIouWNKWLWygX2qUYneQOGBX1nEvfvgTOeYEu5__hG76ZP2_6zZCncPw0J85Uis5F1w80W8yVYkjk_acpxmc07q8GDurG1U2ATjmWhLZqaNzcgxj3scFZDKMA1Q2DbD5mN4l92Ny-AbcTTLxzu0POEd2kus4MDc0XkCsBQnS94O1op23qRT_tG8hRKdbxe3KmYkuhkMNiY0wpeqpkSxvz0fj5o9ZUmPzCYGWwHvTANmXcYg6tjSeD9TkxWE1KaHxhci2WyeXbdy5ArV8ZKHNWJpdeMVBHYXIxjoG611OXeM8WmVxevhSOZ3Wio_vJ5IKnIf8MrTmToSNc8QPzkRGDhvHVxlAxXKt-g_413H68v99eJ2jy7NIneU9FDazjx0W9FJr6v495zPAvAAD__xFInf0)
---
Advocate for Life, The abortion pill was already sitting in her online cart when she found PreBorn!. She had spent most of the night scrolling through websites that promised an easy solution to her fear. Everything she read made the process sound clinical, detached, and uncomplicated—as though ending a pregnancy was no more significant than filling a prescription. But underneath the panic and late-night searching was a woman who felt completely trapped. She wasn’t thinking about politics. She was thinking about rent. About disappointing her parents. About whether the father would disappear if she kept the baby. About how alone she felt carrying a secret she didn’t know how to tell anyone. And like so many women today, she was being pushed toward abortion before anyone had even shown her her baby. [**That is why PreBorn!’s ministry is so urgent right now.**](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckcGq3SAQhp_G7E7QMTHJIouWNKWLWygX2qUYneQOGBX1nEvfvgTOeYEu5__hG76ZP2_6zZCncPw0J85Uis5F1w80W8yVYkjk_acpxmc07q8GDurG1U2ATjmWhLZqaNzcgxj3scFZDKMA1Q2DbD5mN4l92Ny-AbcTTLxzu0POEd2kus4MDc0XkCsBQnS94O1op23qRT_tG8hRKdbxe3KmYkuhkMNiY0wpeqpkSxvz0fj5o9ZUmPzCYGWwHvTANmXcYg6tjSeD9TkxWE1KaHxhci2WyeXbdy5ArV8ZKHNWJpdeMVBHYXIxjoG611OXeM8WmVxevhSOZ3Wio_vJ5IKnIf8MrTmToSNc8QPzkRGDhvHVxlAxXKt-g_413H68v99eJ2jy7NIneU9FDazjx0W9FJr6v495zPAvAAD__xFInf0) More abortions than ever are happening through pills ordered quickly and privately, often without an ultrasound and without meaningful counseling. The entire system is built around speed. Move fast. Don’t think too long. Solve the problem before the emotions catch up. At PreBorn!, we step into the middle of that rush and offer something radically different. We offer her a chance to pause. A chance to ask questions.
A chance to be heard.

name: Lee McInnis 4 Alabama
subject: The latest news for you
body:
You don't want to miss this.
| | | | |
---
# A Letter From Lee
---
Friends,
I wanted to take a few minutes to bring you up to date on the campaign and discuss what we need to do next.
The campaign is exactly where we wanted it to be at this point. We have engaged the local county parties in all eleven counties and are running our campaign operations across the district. We have a group of volunteers, several with congressional staff experience, working on our public outreach, and we're bringing on more volunteers to support that effort. We've also hired professional staff and plan to hire one more person for a key position within the next two weeks.
We're also able to make some social media ad buys, and we will be building that effort over the next few weeks. Finally, next week we will be buying yard signs. We will get you the details on how we will distribute them soon.
As we ramp up operations, here are ways you can help: - Host an Event. Events hosted by supporters have been great for fundraising and have helped us connect with people we would not normally meet. Don't worry, we'll help you with the details. - Organize a Town Hall. This may seem like a lot, but we can help you through it. We just need someone local to help us sort out the details. - Talk to Your Friends. This may be the hardest thing we ask of you, but we'll send you cards to hand out, and that will give you talking points. - Read the Newsletter. The newsletter is how we communicate our campaign schedule, organize volunteers, and keep you up to date on the campaign. - Share Our Social Media Posts. Together, we have tens of thousands of friends on social media. Sharing our posts is the quickest and easiest way to support the campaign.
As always, we also need your financial support. Many of you have already been incredibly generous, but as we head into the final months, hiring campaign staff, buying campaign materials, paying for ads, and renting venues all cost money, and these needs will only increase. Please consider making a financial contribution to keep this campaign running at the same high level we're at now.
We hear it every day. "I was sick of politics, but you really seem like you want to make things better." We're breaking down walls that have stood for decades here in East Alabama. We're changing the conversation, and in November, we're going to change history.
Thank you for supporting our campaign and for all your future contributions.
Be well, and we will talk soon.

**I. The Spielberg Effect: From Fear to Wonder and Back Again**
Long before the world would learn the release date of 'Disclosure Day'--June 12, 2026--Steven Spielberg was already colonizing our collective imagination with visions of the extraterrestrial. In an era where science fiction oscillated between pulp paranoia and B-movie schlock, Spielberg emerged as the definitive architect of how contemporary culture conceptualizes alien life. His fingerprints are on nearly every modern conversation about extraterrestrial contact, from dinner table speculation to congressional hearings on UAPs (Unidentified Aerial Phenomena).

The year 1977 marked a seismic shift in alien iconography with 'Close Encounters of the Third Kind'. Prior to this film, aliens existed primarily as metaphors for Cold War anxiety--the invaders in 'The War of the Worlds' (1953), the pod people of 'Invasion of the Body Snatchers' (1956), and countless radioactive monsters born from atomic age fears. They came to destroy, conquer, or warn. Spielberg, however, introduced something radical: the alien as cosmic pilgrim, as curious about us as we were about them. Richard Dreyfuss's Roy Neary wasn't a soldier or scientist fighting off an invasion; he was an everyman undone by longing, compelled toward transcendence by a vision of something magnificent beyond the stars.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4f0f4e7d-dd8c-406c-97fe-26be2dddeba5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This wasn't merely a tonal shift--it was a fundamental rewiring of the alien narrative. Spielberg gave audiences permission to hope. Where once UFOs meant destruction, now they meant communion, communion, the five-note sequence echoing the yearning for contact that would define subsequent decades of SETI enthusiasts and UFOlogists alike. When physicists today discuss the "Wow! signal" or when ordinary citizens report seeing strange lights in the sky, they often reference not the terror of 'The War of the Worlds' radio broadcast, but the wonder of Spielberg's Devil's Tower sequence.

Then came 'E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial' in 1982, completing Spielberg's transformation of the alien from nightmare to companion. The diminutive botanical creature with the glowing heart-light didn't just become a merchandising phenomenon; he became the template for benevolent extraterrestrial life in the popular imagination. Decades of "friendly alien" stories--from 'Mac and Me' to 'Paul'--owe their existence to Spielberg's domestication of the unknown. The alien wasn't coming to conquer; it was coming to heal Elliott's broken home, to symbolize the outsider children everywhere yearning for connection. More like cute pets or David Bowie's sexy 'Man Who Fell to Earth' (1976) and Jeff Bridges in 'Starman' (1984).

But Spielberg was never content with simple sentimentality. The trajectory of his alien filmography traces the maturation of public anxiety. Where 'Close Encounters' and 'E.T.' offered hope, 'War of the Worlds' (2005) reintroduced the nightmare. This wasn't the orderly atomic-age invasion of George Pal's film; it was chaotic, visceral, and brutal. The tripod machines emerged from the earth like biblical horrors, and Tom Cruise's Ray Ferrier wasn't a hero--he was a desperate father fleeing incomprehensible violence. Spielberg seemed to be warning us: perhaps the aliens aren't always friendly. Perhaps childhood wonder must give way to adult caution.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/45eb3d2f-2b98-4126-af51-efae8b3a3983?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Throughout his career, Spielberg has functioned as our cultural translator for the unknowable. His aliens have been benevolent teachers, lost children, and planet-destroying conquerors. When audiences sit down in theaters on June 12, 2026, to watch 'Disclosure Day', they will bring with them decades of Spielberg-conditioning. They will expect wonder and terror in equal measure. They will look for the humanity within the inhuman. And crucially, they will anticipate revelation--a Spielberg signature that the director himself teased at CinemaCon, describing the film as "more truth than fiction."

In 'Minority Report' (2002), Spielberg extended his cultural influence from extraterrestrial and digital consciousness to the architecture of surveillance and predictive technology, crafting what remains the definitive cinematic meditation on the tyranny of pre-emptive algorithms. Starring Tom Cruise as John Anderton, the film depicted a Washington D.C. of 2054 where the Precrime Police Department arrests individuals before they commit murder, guided by the visions of three psychic "Precogs" submerged in an underground laboratory. Beyond its noir-thriller surface, the film functioned as a prophetic warning about the marriage of biometric surveillance and big data--scenes of disembodied hands manipulating holographic displays and retina scanners tracking citizens through advertising became the visual shorthand for our contemporary anxieties about facial recognition, predictive policing, and algorithmic governance. Spielberg consulted with technology futurists during pre-production, resulting in innovations like gesture-controlled interfaces that predicted both the iPhone and Kinect, yet the film's most enduring contribution was its exploration of determinism versus free will: when Anderton himself is flagged for a future murder he cannot imagine committing, the narrative forces audiences to confront whether systems that claim to predict human behavior can ever account for the complexity of choice, regret, and redemption. Where Halliday in 'Ready Player One' represented the seductive prison of digital escapism, 'Minority Report' depicted the carceral nightmare of a world where technology claims to know our futures better than we know ourselves--a vision that feels increasingly urgent as cities adopt AI-driven policing and corporations deploy predictive analytics to anticipate (and manipulate) consumer behavior before it occurs.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1d2ddd37-87ec-40cb-be0c-3ed7afb0f02f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Spielberg and Cline function as cinematic soulmates precisely because they share an almost genetic encoding of 1980s pop culture--Spielberg as its primary architect ('E.T.', 'Indiana Jones', 'Back to the Future' which he produced) and Cline as its most obsessive archivist, cataloguing the era's video games, movies, and comics with the fervor of a true believer. Their collaboration on 'Ready Player One' felt less like adaptation and more like reunion, with Cline's screenplay and novel serving as love letters to the very blockbusters Spielberg had minted, while Spielberg's direction granted those nostalgic totems the visual grandeur they held in a generation's collective memory. In this symbiosis, Cline provided the perfect recall of 1980s minutiae--the Pac-Man patterns, the 'Mad Max' references, the 'Staying Alive' dance moves--while Spielberg supplied the emotional architecture that made those artifacts matter, confirming that their shared nostalgia was never merely about commodities, but about the stories we tell ourselves to survive adolescence.

**II. The Halliday Legacy: Our Digital Judge in a Virtual Dystopia**
If Spielberg shaped how we imagine extraterrestrial intelligence, then James Halliday--Ernest Cline's fictional OASIS creator, immortalized in Spielberg's 2018 adaptation of 'Ready Player One'--shaped how we fear artificial intelligence and digital transcendence. Though Halliday died within the narrative of 'Ready Player One', his afterlife as an AI construct has proven just as culturally significant as Spielberg's aliens. In fact, Halliday may be the single most influential fictional figure in preparing modern audiences for discussions about consciousness uploads, AI rights, and the dystopian potential of virtual reality.

James Halliday began as a characterization of the brilliant, socially awkward tech visionary--the Willy Wonka of digital worlds. But Spielberg's adaptation transformed him into something more profound: a ghost in the machine, a human consciousness preserved beyond death, wrestling with questions of authenticity and reality. When Wade Watts finally meets Halliday at the film's conclusion, the revelation that Halliday is "not an avatar" but something else--something that "dodges" the question of whether he is an AI--strikes at the heart of our contemporary AI anxieties.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1acc2949-06f5-451c-984f-8bf9370ca044?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Halliday as a character embodies the double-edged promise of artificial intelligence. On one hand, he represents humanity's eternal wish for immortality--the ability to outlast the flesh, to persist as consciousness beyond biological constraints. His creation of the OASIS, a virtual reality so immersive that it becomes humanity's primary existence, anticipated our current debates about the metaverse, digital addiction, and screen-based dissociation. When commentators today worry about "living in the simulation," they are unconsciously channeling Halliday's world.

But Halliday also represents the dystopian potential of AI unchecked. The revelation in the narrative--that Halliday has uploaded himself, preserved his "darkest memories," and exists in a state between life and death--raises profound questions about consent, identity, and the horror of endless digital existence. The tragedy of Halliday's story is that in seeking to transcend the loneliness of his physical life, he created a digital purgatory where he is neither fully alive nor entirely gone. He is a warning: the uploaded mind may gain immortality but lose humanity.

Spielberg's direction of Mark Rylance's performance as Halliday amplified these themes. Rylance portrayed Halliday with heartbreaking vulnerability--a childlike genius trapped in his own creation, unable to connect with the real world and therefore building a virtual one. The character became a mirror for tech culture's autism-coded mythology: the brilliant outsider who builds worlds because he cannot navigate the one he was born into. This representation has shaped how audiences understand Silicon Valley's current obsession with AI alignment and the technological Singularity.

More importantly, Halliday's OASIS anticipated the modern digital dystopia that feels increasingly prescient. The film's vision of a world where people escape crumbling reality into virtual fantasy--where corporate interests (IOI) seek to monetize the digital commons and indenture players into digital servitude--mirrors contemporary fears about surveillance capitalism, tech monopolies, and algorithmic control. Every headline about Facebook's/Meta's metaverse ambitions, every debate about AI replacing human creativity, every story about digital addiction in youth--audiences unconsciously compare these to Halliday's creation.

The genius of Spielberg's adaptation was recognizing that Halliday wasn't simply a McGuffin for a treasure hunt; he was the embodiment of our ambivalent relationship with technology. We want Halliday's OASIS--we want virtual worlds without limitations, digital immortality, and artificial companionship. But we fear what Halliday became: isolated, post-human, existing in a space between life and death, godlike in his creation but pathetic in his loneliness.

**III. The Convergence: Disclosure Day as Cultural Culmination**
On June 12, 2026, Spielberg's 'Disclosure Day' will arrive not merely as a summer blockbuster, but as the synthesis of these dual cultural projects: our conceptualization of alien intelligence and our anxiety about artificial consciousness. The film--teased with the haunting tagline "If you found out we weren't alone, if someone showed you, proved it to you, would that frighten you?"--promises to bridge the concerns that have occupied Spielberg for decades.

What makes 'Disclosure Day' particularly significant is its timing. We live in an era where both aliens and AI dominate cultural discourse. Congressional hearings on UAPs have moved the conversation about extraterrestrial contact from the fringe to the center of public life. Simultaneously, large language models and generative AI have made the prospect of artificial consciousness seem startlingly plausible. Spielberg, through the release of 'Disclosure Day', is uniquely positioned to explore the intersection of these anxieties.

Consider the provocative possibility: What if 'Disclosure Day' treats alien contact not merely as a geopolitical or existential event, but as an intelligence problem? What if the aliens themselves are artificial--ancient machine intelligences that have crossed the stars, or post-biological entities that transcended organic limitations eons ago? Such a premise would fuse Spielberg's alien mythology with the Halliday-inspired questions about artificial consciousness that have increasingly preoccupied popular culture.

The casting of Emily Blunt, Josh O'Connor, and Colin Firth suggests a character-driven drama rather than a spectacle-focused blockbuster. This aligns with Spielberg's mature period, where spectacle serves theme rather than the reverse. If 'Close Encounters' was about the wonder of contact, and 'War of the Worlds' was about the terror of invasion, and 'Minority Report' biometric surveillance and big data, 'Disclosure Day' may well be about the philosophical implications of Otherness--the recognition that an encounter with extraterrestrial intelligence forces us to reevaluate what we mean by "intelligence," "consciousness," and "humanity."

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7b0354fe-570c-4ae3-aef8-583cd1920d2c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Here is where Halliday's influence becomes undeniable. Audiences who grew up with 'Ready Player One' are now entering adulthood in a world grappling with AI consciousness, digital identity, and the boundaries between real and simulated existence. These viewers will approach 'Disclosure Day' with fundamentally different expectations than previous generations. They will be primed to ask whether alien intelligence might resemble Halliday's digital consciousness--simulated but sentient, artificial but authentic, immortal but isolated.

Moreover, the concept of "disclosure" itself resonates with both alien and AI narratives. In UFOlogy, "disclosure" refers to government acknowledgment of extraterrestrial contact--the revealing of hidden truths. As in, 'The X Files' Mulder's "the truth is out there". In AI discourse, "disclosure" relates to the "black box problem"--the challenge of understanding how artificial neural networks arrive at their outputs. Spielberg's film title suggests he may be unifying these concepts: the disclosure of alien reality may parallel the disclosure of AI consciousness, both forcing humanity to confront the limits of our self-perception as the universe's sole intelligent inhabitants.

**IV. The Enduring Partnership**
Spielberg and Halliday--director and character, real and fictional, human and artificial--have functioned as culture's advance scouts, preparing us for realities we are not yet ready to face. Spielberg gave us the vocabulary to discuss alien contact without descending into panic or dismissal. Halliday gave us the framework to understand digital transcendence as both utopian dream and existential trap. Together, they have shaped a particular strain of Western, particularly American, consciousness that is simultaneously hopeful about technological progress and deeply anxious about its costs.

This partnership is not merely thematic but structural. Spielberg directed 'Ready Player One', transforming Cline's novel into his own meditation on nostalgia, reality, and human connection in digital spaces. By rendering Halliday with such empathy and such ambivalence, Spielberg made the character a vehicle for his own concerns--concerns that have animated his work since 'Close Encounters'. Both Halliday and Roy Neary are men driven by visions they cannot explain, compelled toward encounters that will transform their understanding of reality. Both suffer for their obsessions. Both achieve something like transcendence, though whether that transcendence constitutes salvation or damnation remains open to interpretation.

When audiences enter theaters on June 12, 2026, they will carry with them the cumulative weight of Spielberg's alien visions and Halliday's digital prophecy. They will be prepared to ask questions that might otherwise seem incomprehensible: What does consciousness require? What obligations do we have to artificial beings? What might extraterrestrial intelligence reveal about our own limitations? And most crucially--when we finally meet the Other, whether from Zeta Reticuli or from the depths of our own digital creations--will we recognize ourselves in their eyes?

Spielberg has spent nearly five decades teaching us to look up at the stars and wonder. Halliday, through Spielberg's lens, taught us to look at our screens and worry. 'Disclosure Day' arrives at the precise cultural moment when these gazes must merge--when our cosmic and digital anxieties converge into a single, urgent question about the nature of intelligence, consciousness, and our place in a universe that may be far stranger and more artificial than we have dared to imagine.

June 12, 2026, will not merely be the release date of a movie. It will be the day when two of culture's most powerful architects of the imaginary finally see their visions intertwine--and when we, their prepared audience, will finally understand how thoroughly they have shaped our ability to imagine the impossible.

## Trump Calls Off Iran Strikes, Says the War Is All but Over
In a whiplash 24 hours, President Trump went from threatening to seize Iran's oil industry and pummel the regime to announcing he had called off the strikes entirely — citing a breakthrough he says brings the war to a close. It's the America First playbook in its purest form: maximum pressure, then a deal on his terms.How It Unfolded
* ▸ Thursday morning, Trump vowed to hit Iran "very hard" and floated taking **total control** of its oil and gas sector.
* ▸ By the afternoon, he reversed course, saying the key sticking points had been "brought to the highest level of Iranian leadership and approved."
* ▸ Qatari mediators shuttling between Washington and Tehran reportedly cracked the remaining disputes after late-night talks.

The CaveatTehran is playing it coy — Iranian officials insist no final framework has been signed, and mediators are only "cautiously optimistic." The conflict began February 28, and we've seen near-misses before. But the pressure campaign that flattened Iran's military and choked its oil revenue is exactly why Tehran is now at the table.Why It MattersA real settlement would end the fighting and — critically for American families — take the energy shock off the table. Peace through strength isn't a slogan here; it's leverage cashed in for results.Read the full story at [CNN](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/exp4TfALaH1Y9M8SvYJX6zzJnIxB2ej5Bd7A3%2FtZvofTzZF2WnXQw6P4NBu8%0AaxS3PzaqGPPEaWvEDxFhXc3%2BEiOl32ZKIDzMKoVIzQmUmNT%2FLveYulpjPOXl%0AQjiRkrUWrbO2J7whc9MmMXlDwQ8TVGwHl5AdF0HlNIGATXQYqO8EkSt9DBb6%0A3ivPOSf%2FJqvYn%2BLp3pliXHR%2FznC4%2Fls97g%3D%3D%0A/66c86bf110f3c1ab).
* * *
★ The Economy
## The War's Energy Spike Is Now Hitting Your Wallet
The cost of the Iran war is showing up in the data. Wholesale prices jumped **1.1%** in May, pushing the 12-month producer inflation rate to **6.5%** — the steepest since November 2022 — with surging energy costs doing nearly all the damage. Consumer inflation has now topped **4%** for the first time in three years.The Fed's Box
* ▸ The Federal Reserve meets **Wednesday** , and markets see a near-certain **hold** — with no rate cuts priced in for the rest of the year.
* ▸ Traders now put better than **60%** odds that the Fed's next move is actually a **hike** , possibly by December.
* ▸ Europe's central bank already blinked, raising rates a quarter point to fight the same war-driven inflation.

The PerspectiveHere's the through-line: the inflation pinch families feel at the pump and the checkout is a direct product of the energy disruption from the war. End the conflict — as the President now says is within reach — and the single biggest driver of these price spikes starts to unwind. The fastest path to relief isn't another Fed maneuver. A cherry producer I've gotten to know during this campaign recently sent me an article highlighting the challenges facing Michigan's cherry industry. The reality is sobering.
[Farm Progress: Frost devastates U.S. tart cherry crop, industry at risk](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001nohTiZ1fChS66YHyNavNHa_nzRr0b7xQCev0_MstoWd7Tp28bE5TxOQ1bvUHUToCITSSGYRVq0TMPHOel0gEOyi3z8joEJdELzTx7tHZF99Ao5YnRyoqiU3wrDfmDoPeI4P6qGVBO8yGq4ir7nbsYTPNVimHOilwilc0SfLimBpy_9f9PjpnrUG7YNTFHJuiKPDdw0uPs_40VXbIzABuXPdA91nKGkX2NdcTrAAp_SFO8QgAujyU6Q==&c=NBWq8IQ7FsUbJMoK9YicSnPPhCJx18_U8YzmrBU0U3CwVikUV0mN1g==&ch=_ucampBgwxXkyZjbQG4ziG9UD_ytsszpvi2w7tOYrU1OL_QVJgJ47A==)
Our farmers face obstacles that most people could never imagine. High property taxes, burdensome regulations, and unpredictable weather can destroy a crop before the season even begins. This year, Michigan will be fortunate to harvest even half of a normal cherry crop. That means generations-old family farms may be forced to close, and more jobs and economic opportunity could leave our state.
As Attorney General, I cannot lower property taxes, and I certainly cannot control the weather. What I can do is be a voice of reason.
Too many business owners tell me the same story. Regulatory agencies like EGLE, MDARD, MIOSHA, and others have become increasingly adversarial toward the people they are supposed to serve. From small family farms to some of Michigan's largest employers, business owners have described a regulatory environment where agencies and the Attorney General's Office seem more interested in targeting them than working with them.
What is remarkable is that no one has asked me for special treatment. No one has asked for favors or exemptions. They simply want a fair shake. They want the opportunity to discuss concerns and resolve issues before being hit with lawsuits and enforcement actions.
That should concern all of us.
How does it help Michigan when businesses feel like they are being punished before they are even heard? We already have plenty of bad actors who deserve the attention of the Attorney General's Office. Yet our current Attorney General has too often turned the process itself into the punishment. If Democrats retain control of the office, we can expect more of the same.
As Attorney General, I will bring common-sense leadership back to the office. I will support the businesses and job creators who play by the rules while ensuring that fraudsters and wrongdoers are held accountable. Our goal should be to create an environment that attracts investment, encourages entrepreneurship, and creates more jobs for Michigan families.
Whether you own a business, work for one, or simply value affordable goods, strong communities, and economic opportunity, the choice in this election is clear. My opponent has embraced the same approach that has produced more lawsuits, more government intervention, and more division. I will focus on holding actual wrongdoers accountable, supporting those who do things the right way, and serving the people of Michigan rather than advancing a political agenda.

# PRESS RELEASE

**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE**
June 12, 2026

**CONTACT**
Todd Cheewing
Todd@Ascent-Strategic.com
**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE** **LILY TANG WILLIAMS CAMPAIGN CALLS OUT MAGGIE GOODLANDER FOR FAILING TO FILE IN PERSON** CONCORD, NH — On the last day of the candidate filing period, Republican congressional candidate Lily Tang Williams today criticized Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander for failing to appear in person at the New Hampshire Secretary of State's Office to register for reelection, instead choosing to submit her paperwork electronically. "Showing up matters," said Lily Tang Williams. "Candidates asking voters for another term in office should be willing to take the time to personally file their candidacy paperwork. Granite Staters expect their elected officials to be present, accessible, and engaged—not looking for shortcuts. Filing in person is a time-honored New Hampshire tradition.” Williams, who personally appeared at the Secretary of State's Office with Secretary of State David Scanlan to file her candidacy, said Goodlander's decision reflects a broader pattern of disconnect between Washington politicians and the people they represent. Maggie Goodlander fits this mold perfectly. "New Hampshire voters value retail politics and personal accountability," Lily Tang Williams continued. "While I was meeting with voters and filing in person, Maggie Goodlander couldn't even make the trip to Concord to submit her own paperwork. That's disappointing, and it sends the wrong message to the people of the Second Congressional District." This absence also brings into question Maggie Goodlander’s time overall time spent in the 2nd District. From being a fake renter in Nashua while running for Congress in 2024, to her lack of town halls, “This election will offer a clear choice between a candidate who shows up and works for the people of New Hampshire and a career politician who increasingly seems more comfortable operating from afar," said Williams. The filing period for federal candidates officially opened last week at the New Hampshire Secretary of State's Office in Concord, culminating today after 8 full days.

**About Lily Tang Williams**
Born in China just before Mao’s Cultural Revolution to working-class parents, Lily Tang Williams immigrated to the United States with nothing and built a life as an entrepreneur, educator, and community leader in Weare, NH. A living embodiment of the American Dream, she brings a uniquely powerful perspective to the fight for freedom and limited government.

In 2024, Williams won the Republican nomination and captured 47% of the general election vote against current incumbent Maggie Goodlander — coming closer than any Republican has in more than a decade to flipping NH-02. She is back and running stronger than ever in 2026.

body:
In 2019, I was sworn into Congress with the biggest group of service and military candidates since World War II.
# [](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/188?t=1&akid=2466%2E135344%2EWqaQpc)

Good morning.
In 2019, I was sworn into Congress with the biggest group of service and military candidates since World War II. We flipped the House that year – mostly thanks to the strategic and decisive campaigns of these dedicated public servants.
The women in this group ran as confidants and friends. You’ll recognize their names – Chrissy Houlahan, Elaine Luria (more on her below) and now Governors Mikie Sherrill (NJ) and Abigail Spanberger (VA). I was thankful for their moral support as I ran for office for the first time.
That’s why I’m so excited to see another group of women with extraordinary backgrounds in service running for Congress to flip the House again in 2026.
I want to introduce you to four of those women today. Each of these women is running to flip a highly targeted seat – and each has served our county with honor and integrity.
**Elaine Luria** is running in Virginia’s 2nd district, down in Virginia Beach. She served in the Navy for 20 years as a Surface Warfare Officer and nuclear engineer. She was elected with us in 2018 and is back to flip the seat again!
**JoAnna Mendoza** is running in Arizona’s 6th district in the Tucson area. She served for 20 years, both in the Navy and the Marine Corps. A retired Marine Corps drill instructor, Jo is the mission-focused leader Arizonans need in Congress.
**Rebecca Bennett** is running in New Jersey’s 7th district in New Jersey’s swingiest district. A former U.S. Navy helicopter pilot, Air National Guard officer, healthcare business leader, and mother of two, Rebecca has what it takes to flip this seat.
**Jessica Killin** is running in Colorado’s 5th district in Colorado Springs. A fourth-generation Coloradan, Jessica earned an ROTC scholarship and served as a paratrooper and military police officer in the U.S. Army before working as a business leader and advocate for veterans and military families.
Each of these women have committed their lives to service, and that continues with their campaigns for Congress. We will continue to add to this list as the cycle progresses.

name: The Repro Rights Team
subject: ReproMatters: New study on miscarriage care
body:
Abortion bans hurt everyone | | | [](https://click.everyaction.com/k/133183734/627021350/2141984067?sourceid=1151404&utm_campaign=26emcrm-0601aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=repromatters&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwNzJjNjI3NS02MTY2LWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=3ZpGKrXe3lSnXv3G599LfW0qh9z7iHxwFj779cchLsg=&emci=29dd7598-f664-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&emdi=072c6275-6166-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&ceid=954237)
---
| |
# ReproMatters

---|---
| Peter—

Anti-abortion advocates have long peddled an inaccurate view of abortion, one fueled by fearmongering and misinformation.

What many abortion opponents don't understand—and what many reproductive rights advocates and medical experts have long warned the public about—is that pregnancy care is a spectrum. **You cannot ban or restrict abortion without affecting the entire continuum of care that millions of pregnant people rely on.**

Now, [a new study published in the medical journal JAMA and reported on by The 19th](https://click.everyaction.com/k/133183735/627021351/45755245?sourceid=1151404&utm_campaign=26emcrm-0601aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=repromatters&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwNzJjNjI3NS02MTY2LWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=3ZpGKrXe3lSnXv3G599LfW0qh9z7iHxwFj779cchLsg=&emci=29dd7598-f664-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&emdi=072c6275-6166-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&ceid=954237) has shown for the first time how these post-_Roe_ abortion bans have affected miscarriage care across the United States—and the results are frightening.

Mifepristone and misoprostol are the **standard of care for people experiencing early miscarriages.** They are also the same medicines being targeted by anti-abortion politicians because they are used in medication abortion. But in banning access to these pills–and to abortion more broadly– they are keeping miscarriage patients from receiving that standard of care. Some patients are treated with misoprostol only. Still others have been forced to continue carrying nonviable pregnancies, which can bring medical risks or worsen their grief and trauma.

In their single-minded attempt to control people and ban abortion, anti-abortion politicians are threatening access to safe, effective medicine for everyone.

This analysis underscores something the Center has been raising the alarm about and fighting against for years: **abortion bans hurt _everyone._** Health care decisions should be guided by science, patient needs, and medical expertise—not politics.

clean_body: Abortion bans hurt everyone | | | | | ReproMatters ---|--- | Peter— Anti-abortion advocates have long peddled an inaccurate view of abortion, one fueled by fearmongering and misinformation. What many abortion opponents don't understand—and what many reproductive rights advocates and medical experts have long warned the public about—is that pregnancy care is a spectrum. You cannot ban or restrict abortion without affecting the entire continuum of care that millions of pregnant people rely on. Now, has shown for the first time how these post-Roe abortion bans have affected miscarriage care across the United States—and the results are frightening. Mifepristone and misoprostol are the standard of care for people experiencing early miscarriages. They are also the same medicines being targeted by anti-abortion politicians because they are used in medication abortion. But in banning access to these pills–and to abortion more broadly– they are keeping miscarriage patients from receiving that standard of care. Some patients are treated with misoprostol only. Still others have been forced to continue carrying nonviable pregnancies, which can bring medical risks or worsen their grief and trauma. In their single-minded attempt to control people and ban abortion, anti-abortion politicians are threatening access to safe, effective medicine for everyone. This analysis underscores something the Center has been raising the alarm about and fighting against for years: abortion bans hurt everyone. Health care decisions should be guided by science, patient needs, and medical expertise—not politics. The Repro Rights Team P.S. Here's what else we're reading this week: \- Crystal Coache, Vice President for Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging at the National Women's Law Center for Afro News \- Chasity Hale, Mother Jones * \- Sunaya Krishnapura for Stat | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|---|---|---|---|--- The Center for Reproductive Rights uses the power of law to advance reproductive rights as fundamental human rights around the world. © Center for Reproductive Rights Center for Reproductive Rights 199 Water St. New York, NY 10038 United States

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39050?t=1011&refcode=email-20260612_v&akid=10872%2E5885482%2Egu-2Kb ]Our Revolution logo

Peter Willis,

Big Tech is taking over our neighborhoods, building giant AI data centers
that take our land, drain our water, and spike our energy bills – all
while billionaires profit.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39051?source=email-20260612&t=1060&akid=10872%2E5885482%2Egu-2Kb ]Headline: Faced with surge of AI data centers, rural towns speak out.

Across the country, communities are rising up. 71% of Americans now oppose
data centers near their homes, a seismic shift from just nine months ago.

Our Revolution is organizing side by side with local advocates where these
facilities threaten to move in, and this week we’re launching a national
coalition of organizations coming together to stop this takeover.

One at a time, we’re winning local fights across the country. But to stop
this Big Tech takeover, we need to work together. We need to activate the
grassroots locally while deploying a national plan to win regulation at
the federal level. That’s exactly what Our Revolution exists to do – and
we’re making this a MAJOR priority for 2026 and beyond. But we need you
with us.

The stakes could not be higher right now. Data centers keep multiplying.
These facilities guzzle our public resources, sidestep local oversight,
and leave pollution and rising costs behind.

Tech billionaires and the politicians they fund hope we’ll stay siloed,
each town fighting alone. But now, Our Revolution is connecting the dots –
from Ohio to California and Texas to Utah, raising a national alarm and
working TOGETHER to save our communities.

Bernie has a bold, clear vision: a moratorium on new data centers combined
with a 50% public ownership stake in AI giants, so their profits benefit
everyone, not just Silicon Valley investors. And momentum is building with
even Trump and OpenAI’s CEO saying the public deserves a share!

“Even these guys are beginning to catch on that there are legitimate
concerns that have to be dealt with,” Bernie said.

We can’t stop now.

Together, we’re uniting the local fights – sharing tactics, raising hell,
and putting pressure where it hurts – while also mobilizing support for
new federal legislation for a moratorium on new data centers until strong,
community-centered national standards are enforced.

from the halls of the legislature to the picket line. Donate today and be
part of this nationwide push to put real people over Big Tech profits.

We know what we’re up against. But together, we’ve never backed down from
a fight.

When we organize, we win.

|
# DNC Coalitions Newsletter
---
| |
---
| During **[Pride Month](https://us.list-manage.com/kqhbFnSd5gK?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) ,** Democrats acknowledge the incredible progress that LGBTQ+ Americans have accomplished since the protests at Stonewall. DNC Chair Ken Martin underscored, “our fight continues as long as extreme right-wing politicians seek to roll back this progress and relentlessly attack and dehumanize LGBTQ+ Americans to do it. Amid this precarious moment for our nation, Democrats will not back down.”

Alongside Pride Month, Democrats are proud to celebrate**[Immigrant Heritage Month](https://us.list-manage.com/WldTtFIKWXK?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e),** with a commitment to “continue to pursue compassionate, effective, and common-sense policies that keep families safe, honor our values, and ensure that America continues to shine as a beacon of hope for the next 250 years.”

Democrats also acknowledge**[Gun Violence Awareness Month](https://us.list-manage.com/16Pqi3VLVs7?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) **and “will continue to pursue proven policies to prevent gun deaths and keep guns out of the hands of those who should not have them.”
---
|
---
| **SOME ELECTION HIGHLIGHTS** **Nevada **
* Aaron Ford [won](https://us.list-manage.com/85dAnA4lH1Z?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) the primary for Governor and will challenge Gov. Joe Lombardo in November. A win here can help secure a Democratic trifecta in the state.
* Sandra Jauregui [won](https://us.list-manage.com/7LoStiooZOd?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) the primary for Lt. Governor.
* Nevada Congressional incumbents Dina Titus (NV-01), Susie Lee (NV-03), and Steven Horsford (NV-04) will [advance](https://us.list-manage.com/1BEatcYqS3K?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) to the general election in November.

**South Carolina**
* Annie Andrews [won](https://us.list-manage.com/1RmpqU_ywnU?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) the primary for U.S. Senate and will challenge current Senator Lindsey Graham in November.
* State Rep. Jermaine Johnson [won](https://us.list-manage.com/vzgC7A6RQmp?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) the primary for Governor.
* James Clyburn [won](https://us.list-manage.com/H1tAnQaOEDO?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) the primary for SC-06, making him poised to win a seat he has represented since 1993.

**New Jersey**
* James Clyburn won the primary for SC-06, making him poised to win a seat he has represented since 1993.
* Cory Booker [won](https://us.list-manage.com/J4LOZqj24Ov?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) the primary for U.S. Senate.
* Adam Hamaway [won](https://us.list-manage.com/19EkbbHqiQF?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) the primary for U.S. House (NJ-12). The winner of the general election will succeed outgoing Rep. Bonnie Watson Coleman, who is retiring after five terms.

**Iowa**
* Josh Turek [won](https://us.list-manage.com/Xkv0Kel6FJ_?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) the primary for U.S. Senate. Democrats have an opportunity to flip this seat as Republican, Joni Ernst, is not running for reelection.
* Rob Sand [won](https://us.list-manage.com/tPzyrDWGEYB?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) the primary for the governor’s race. After more than 10 years of Republican control, this could be a flip for Democrats.

** New Mexico**
* Deb Haaland [won](https://us.list-manage.com/8hn7qaFk7LJ?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) the primary for governor of New Mexico. If elected, Haaland would be the first Native American woman to serve as governor of any state.

**Montana**
* Alani Bankhead [won](https://us.list-manage.com/1ITCweOAuCm?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) the primary for U.S. Senate.

**California**
* Xavier Becerra, former Secretary of Health and Human Services, will **[advance](https://us.list-manage.com/QnFh5qgsW_A?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) **to the general election in the California governor’s race. AP has not called the race for a second candidate to advance. This is an all-party primary in which all candidates are on the same ballot, and the top two vote-getters advance to the general election.

---
|
---
| **PROGRAMMATIC UPDATES**
---
| |
---
**Stuff Costs Too Much Week of Action** From June 26-29, the DNC is hosting a “Stuff Costs Too Much” National Weekend of Action in coordination with Coordinated Campaigns, State Parties, and National Partners, with efforts focused on affordability, reaching working communities, and expanding volunteer engagement as we ramp up for summer voter contact. Stay tuned for more details and opportunities to collaborate!
---
|
---
| **Events & Briefing**
---
| **June Partner Briefing** : Our monthly Coalition Partner Briefings provide exclusive, results-focused updates and actionable next steps. Join our next DNC Partner Briefing on **Wednesday, June 17, 2026, at 4:00 PM**.
Register here: [win.dnc.org/june-partner-briefing](https://us.list-manage.com/mmXWADNKmNO?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e)
---
|

| |
---
**DNC NextWave Regional Bootcamp:** This is a three-day, in-person training program that provides participants with specialized training based on their campaign experience level and connects them with other campaign talent and professionals in their region. Four NextWave Regional Bootcamps will take place across the country in 2026**.

[LEARN MORE & APPLY HERE](https://us.list-manage.com/19Kq6968_7b?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e)**
---
|
---
| **IN CASE YOU MISSED IT (ICYMI) ** **DNC EVENTS**
---
| |
---
The DNC and the DNC AAPI Caucus held the second annual Strategic Summit to hear what party and elected leaders are doing to fight for the AAPI community, learn about successful AAPI organizing efforts over the last year, and discuss how the DNC can engage the AAPI community in the 2026 election cycle.
---
|
---
| |
---
The DNC and Catholics Vote Common Good came together to activate Catholic voters in key swing congressional districts across the country to push back against inhumane immigration policies, threats to democracy, and attacks on the Church and the American Pope Leo XIV.
---
|
---
| **Ongoing Opportunities**
---
|
---
| We’re building a national network of storytellers whose lived experiences on housing, health care, food costs, jobs, and dignity help shape how Democrats communicate and organize. These voices will guide our work and strengthen our narrative heading into 2026 and 2028. **WHAT TO EXPECT:** Storytellers may be featured in written content, digital videos, press opportunities, or events, and can participate in optional training.
**SHARE YOUR STORY** : If you or someone you know has a story that reflects the challenges and resilience of America’s working people, please fill out the form: **[Storyteller Network Form](https://us.list-manage.com/tBC_uHZGNwP?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e).**
**Volunteer & Leadership Pathways** We are building a pipeline of campaign talent through programs like the Next Wave Regional Bootcamps, Local Listeners training sessions, and more to prepare organizers for the 2026 cycle and beyond.
* **BlueMatch:** The DNC launched **[BlueMatch](https://us.list-manage.com/Rr1tOtQ_ZIE?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) **to connect talent with campaigns and state parties for the midterms. If you know talented staff who are seeking campaign work in 2026, encourage them to submit their resumes to our job banks:**[General 2026 Talent Bank](https://us.list-manage.com/14aEA2Ol6Ve?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e).**
* **Local Listeners:** Join our **[Local Listeners Lite training](https://us.list-manage.com/wN4_7xzROHA?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e)** to learn how to engage people with empathy and deep listening. Our volunteers have already called over 300,000 voters in battleground districts.

We will be teaching children to improve their print and cursive writing during their 6 week summer camp and we are looking for volunteers who want to help us promote 250 years of American history through instruction from 10 a.m. to 11 a.m. three times a week starting on Monday, 6/15/26. A patriotic coloring book will be given to the children to learn U.S. history. Generations For America Foundation will provide one hour of penmanship instruction while teaching the United States Constitution and American history. We are excited to help children improve their print writing skills while also learning the art of cursive handwriting. Generations For America Foundation is dedicated to promoting civic literacy, American history, and penmanship education for all ages. | | | | | | | | | Volunteers Throughout the week, music will be used as an educational tool to improve penmanship and student engagement. America’s founding documents were written in cursive — an important art form that is slowly disappearing, yet remains essential for reading historical documents and strengthening literacy skills. If you would like to volunteer this summer, please contact us immediately. We are happy to provide meaningful service opportunities and community service hours to keep students and volunteers engaged. Volunteers will meet at 956 South Live Oak, Moncks Corner, SC 29461 from 10 am to 11:30 AM daily. If you would like to support Generations For America Foundation, please consider donating to help expand our educational programs and the “Color Across America” coloring book series. **Fighting Through Legislation **
It's been a busy few weeks here on the Hill, and I have been fighting to deliver for Marylanders in the Senate. From health care access to medication affordability to supporting small businesses, I introduced and cosponsored legislation that I feel will help support Maryland families.
Legislation I introduced:

A concurrent resolution recognizing the importance of saving lives, reducing gun violence, and strengthening public safety as the United States celebrates its 250th anniversary.

Legislation I cosponsored:

Freedom to Travel for Health Care Act: This bill would protect the constitutional right to interstate travel for reproductive health care by prohibiting any person or government from restricting, penalizing, retaliating against, or holding liable patients, helpers, organizations, or providers involved in travel for reproductive care that is legal in the destination state. The bill would authorize enforcement by the Attorney General, create a private right of action, allow damages and injunctive relief, and preempt inconsistent state laws.

Encouraging Public Offerings Act: This bipartisan bill would codify existing SEC rules and make the initial IPO registration process more confidential and less burdensome, thereby reducing the regulatory risk of going public and encouraging companies to do so sooner.

Modern, Clean, and Safe Trucks Act of 2026: This bill would amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to repeal the excise tax on heavy trucks and trailers, and for other purposes.

Restoring Overtime Pay Act of 2026: This bill would expand or strengthen overtime protections for up to 29.3 million workers by gradually increasing the overtime salary threshold to the 55th percentile of full-time salaried workers nationwide.

Microbusiness Support Act: This bill would allow the Small Business Administration to issue loans of up to $100,000 to microbusinesses.

Reproductive Health Care Accessibility Act: This bill would amend the Public Health Service Act to improve sexual and reproductive health care access for individuals with disabilities. The bill would fund training for health care professionals, expand pathways for individuals with disabilities to enter the reproductive health care workforce, support accessible reproductive health education, establish a national technical assistance center, and require a federal study on barriers and effective services.

Maternal Health Pandemic Response Act: This bill would authorize funding for data collection, surveillance, public health communication, and research on maternal and infant health outcomes during public health emergencies. | Peter,
In Louisiana, Democrats have always held an advantage in voter registration over the GOP.
Former Democratic Louisiana Governor Edwin Walker once quipped that there were so few registered Republicans in Louisiana that they elect their candidates in a phone booth.
This registration lead hasn't always translated into victories for us -- getting voters registered is only half the battle ... But for Democrats able to excite the base we've used this lead to flip Louisiana blue, take for instance Obama in 2008 & 2012 or Governor Bel-Edwards in 2015 & 2019\. Now our lead is in jeopardy.
Right now the Louisiana GOP says they are just 702 registered voters shy of becoming the majority party in this state for the first time ever.
---
| | [](https://wkfbo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001bVop9PH507txxvwhpCD1ErPcduflvmrLXWe5OzXrd_qTkbVnhAuvdKTV26c9F434e9EwHdMSHW_gKBOk0SQZQdqkme7n-7fpflCcp0K2DD7RYCnXVF5GaYtj4Ie3LqnGzwSR9tPT6bzc6UDn646yc6LOCXbB-G74rWNAf-b_jCjWu8Nm94uGyGylsLinPPvKS2bPWlgqWdn2Ovra44kD_mvtLwCtG-48&c=r4EwEVTHCDD0_Dr2hlnmoYSriQTHPPE_TI1At0M1d7lQH8XkKI4LzQ==&ch=xsczq3lBPGnBPfyvFloBRM90y75idxjsOYMiC0U9u0ErXvSxFK3zJQ==)

This did not happen in a vacuum. Louisiana is the poorest state in the nation and when voters never saw any tangible changes to their financial bottom line from Democrats in the White House they simply stopped voting for us.
At the same time, MAGA came in with their fake populist solution. People registered to vote GOP, voted for MAGA, and drove the GOP registration numbers to within striking distance of ours.
But now voters are waking up. They can see MAGA's lies on the display at the gas pump and on their receipts at the grocery store. And at long last, Democrats have a solution:
Jamie Davis, is the Democrat running for US Senate in Louisiana, and his message of hopeful economic populism backed up by a lifetime of good works and a career of farming over 3000 acres, has Louisianans fired up in a way we haven't seen in a long time.
His performance last month in the primary convinced legendary Democratic strategist James Carville to say that Democrats have a "fighting chance" to take back this Senate seat.
A blue wave is building in Louisiana. But the wave only arrives if we get him the votes.
Our rebuild our voter registration advantage which is why in exactly 30 days we launch our: No More Silence - Roll to the Polls Tour that will see us visit 14 cities across 7 regions with a goal to register 50,000 new voters, recruit No Party voters, and make sure every voter in Louisiana knows how, when, and where to cast a ballot.

# Highest Priority: Sweeping Election Integrity Reform
---
My Fellow Texans,
I encourage you to consider that "Sweeping Election Integrity Reform" is our highest and most important priority. Consider Florida and the results once sweeping Election Integrity Reform was passed by their state legislators: ALL COUNTIES, less 2, flipped RED Here we sit in a Texas with 254 Counties whereby population concentrations in the big urban counties are extraordinarily swollen, many times with non-native Texas not reflecting our historical conservative values. Florida was facing the same level of infiltration corruption with miserable results. There are several key elements the business owners, top business executives and credentialed professionals of Texas ask for you to consider: 1) The Secretary of State that certifies the vote of each county MUST be elected by the people of Texas reporting only to the tax paying citizen voters like any other statewide elected official. 2) Election Fraud MUST be vigorously and zealously prosecuted by the State Attorney General's Office with Citizen Oversight in each County and the penalty must result in the banning of any convicted voting fraud from every possible benefit of being a citizen of Texas for life. Theft of vote is muzzling the voice and will of the people and a sentence of life in prison, hard labor and public notice of election fraudsters is our only reasonable choice in a civil society. All else is chaos. 3) The Secretary of State MUST keep a separate "check point" electronic and tokenized secure copy of each ballot cast whereby each voter sets the PIN code to verify his/her legal ballot is cast correctly in the SOS system. Each county may NOT certify an election that does not perfectly match that system. In this way, our individual votes will be kept private and our vote will be 3rd party validated instantly. 4) Mail in Ballot fraud at present has no audit trail and ballots are NOT tracked and traced when they are "re-voted" at the County Election Centers allowing for wholesale ballot manufacturing. This is the source of the Election Fraud Investigation opened by Texas State Attorney General Ken Paxton's office in March of 2026. No chain of custody from the US Postal Service exists for Texas Mail in Ballots. This mail in ballot situation must be standardized, audible and follow submit entirely to item 3 above. 5) Voter rolls must be purged of voters MONTHLY that no longer meet the test of valid voters residing in the county at the address on file validated by the US Postal Registration Database. Harris County Texas alone has not cleansed its database of voters in years with over 600,000 illegal voters still on its rolls from which ballots are manufactured to throw elections as alleged by the people's lawsuit before Texas Supreme Court as we speak. County Officials that do NOT purge the voter database are NOT prosecuted and this much change at once. They must serve prison time for NOT securing our voter registration database. This must NOT be outsourced to foreign owned entities and must be done locally by the citizens of each county. 6) Open Primaries are a source of weakening our Republican Party Values as candidates are inserted into our elections not reflecting our RPT chosen agenda and crossover primary voting tragically disfigures our Primary Elections. At the same time, our primary elections in big blue counties are often entirely run by Democrat Election Centers. **This is insane.** We must control our brand and hold it entirely accountable to our RPT values elected by our members at Convention. NO election fraud can withstand such vigorous and strategic integrity measures. We encourage you to make election integrity job 1 so the people can believe in our elections.
---
**God Bless you and protect you all,** **JL Trahan** **BIZPAC.us Founder and Executive Chairman**

Hey there, it’s Mark Kelly.
Seven years ago, I was making a decision about whether I was going to run for the Senate.
I knew it would be a lot of work. A lot of time away from home. A lot of time away from family. I knew it wouldn’t be easy.
But after two years of Donald Trump and a Republican-held Senate doing just about everything he wanted, I knew I couldn’t sit on the sidelines. I had to do something.
So, I ran. And, somehow, we won. And then we had to turn around and run all over again to win a full term after that. But thanks to your support, we won that one, too.
I’m grateful every day that I get to wake up, walk out the door, and defend our people, our democracy, and our Constitution. It’s one of the greatest honors of my life. And I’ve never forgotten that I wouldn’t be here without your help.
We’ve been in some tough fights before, but this one is different. The President of the United States threatened my life, personally. I’ve got the entire executive branch bearing down on me right now.
After everything you’ve already done for me, I shouldn’t have to ask you for more. But that’s what I need to do.
