# [GSA sells the Old Post Office Building that was formerly Trump Hotel DC](https://substack.com/redirect/a93be760-0a95-44dc-86d3-a1d93af528ba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The General Services Administration **[sold the Old Post Office Building on Pennsylvania Avenue in Washington, D.C](https://substack.com/redirect/7bca6930-dafd-40f5-a112-e5e4f3a6d9db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**. the former site of the Trump International Hotel, to BDT & MSD Partners under the existing ground lease.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a93be760-0a95-44dc-86d3-a1d93af528ba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Eighty Million Dollar Sale:** BDT & MSD Partners acquired the building and land for $80 million dollars and is discussing resale for $400 million.
* **Preservation Covenants Included:** Sale permanently secures public clock tower access and binding protections for the building's architectural heritage.
* **Fine Arts Retained:** Dedicated covenant keeps American public ownership of artwork inside, including Robert Irwin's Forty Eight Shadow Planes and Benjamin Franklin statue.
* **Taxpayer Revenue Gain:** Over $250 million dollars in private capital invested since redevelopment; revenues now exceed $110 million dollars in the last decade.

# [Mamdani backs candidate who called America a "Fu**ing Disgrace"](https://substack.com/redirect/c7ae32c7-9d19-4ab6-a512-08f4a25455b4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani continues endorsing Democratic Socialist congressional candidate Darializa Avila Chevalier for New York's 13th district **[despite resurfaced deleted posts calling America a f***ing disgrace and other radical views.](https://substack.com/redirect/e6e21aeb-69a2-44b6-b2ef-0988613aa8b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c7ae32c7-9d19-4ab6-a512-08f4a25455b4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Views Have Evolved:** Mamdani claims he never saw the old social media posts and states Avila Chevalier's positions have changed since she called veterans war criminals and demanded abolishing borders.
* **Anti Israel Organizer:** Candidate's main credential is leading Columbia University protests featuring assaults on Jewish students and swastikas that forced campus closure.
* **Scrubbed Campaign Pledges:** Website once promised votes against all weapons to any country and nationalizing utilities; language removed for clarity per spokesperson.
* **June Twenty Three Primary:** Mamdani sticks with the DSA insurgent challenging five term Democrat Rep. Adriano Espaillat despite her past praise of his mayoral run.

# [California Took 81 % of Federal immigrant welfare spending](https://substack.com/redirect/c7ae32c7-9d19-4ab6-a512-08f4a25455b4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Federal data shows California received six hundred seventeen point five million dollars--**[eighty one percent of nationwide TANF child only cash assistance](https://substack.com/redirect/686538db-2188-4471-a124-3a0d1dbf2e86?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** tied to immigration status ineligible households--in fiscal year twenty twenty four.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c7ae32c7-9d19-4ab6-a512-08f4a25455b4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Sixty Thousand Households:** Nearly 60,000 California cases represented about 70% of the national total for these immigration related child only TANF benefits.
* **Bypasses Work Rules:** Child only structure allows ongoing household support without the work requirements or 60 month lifetime limits imposed on citizen families.
* **Monthly Benefit Doubled:** Average payment rose from $408 in fiscal 2013 to $875 in fiscal 2024.
* **Cumulative Cost Eighteen Billion:** Since 2001 these cases have totaled roughly $18.3 billion dollars with 4 out of 5 dollars flowing to California.

# [Meta begins dismantling $2 Billion Manus deal on Beijing'd orders](https://substack.com/redirect/c7ae32c7-9d19-4ab6-a512-08f4a25455b4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Meta Platforms has **[completed an operational split](https://substack.com/redirect/78f9483d-60b3-47a6-b4fd-570dcd62d5e1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** from its $2 billion dollar Manus acquisition and suspended data sharing after Beijing ordered the deal reversed under foreign investment security rules.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c7ae32c7-9d19-4ab6-a512-08f4a25455b4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Operational Split Ordered:** Employees stopped using Manus tools internally while blocking the Singapore based firm from accessing Meta's data systems this month.
* **Unprecedented Reversal:** Chinese regulators in April demanded full unwind of the completed acquisition involving strategic AI talent and technology.
* **Tightened Export Controls:** Beijing issued new rules effective July first giving state retroactive chokehold on outbound deals involving Chinese investors or sensitive sectors.
* **Singapore Washing Limits:** Move signals Beijing will not tolerate Chinese origin AI firms relocating headquarters to shed domestic image through foreign acquisitions.

Investor demand for indirect exposure to SpaceX ahead of its one point seven five trillion dollar IPO is **[fueling sharp gains in proxy stocks](https://substack.com/redirect/abe8283d-1ca9-4cf1-9163-46ba5b9b0d64?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and record options trading volumes.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c7ae32c7-9d19-4ab6-a512-08f4a25455b4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **EchoStar Surges Eleven Percent:** The networking firm owning 3% of SpaceX saw options volume eleven times the 30 day average.
* **AST SpaceMobile Up Twelve Percent:** Satellite company with upcoming SpaceX rocket launch recorded nearly $140 million dollars in options activity.
* **ETF Buying Bottleneck:** Funds like Procure UFO and Defiance JEDI are aggressively purchasing shares of AST, EchoStar and Spire due to heavy inflows.
* **Retail Options Explosion:** High implied volatility and short dated call buying reflect both retail and institutional clamor for SpaceX linked plays.

# [GM lets EV owners sell power back to the grid](https://substack.com/redirect/c7ae32c7-9d19-4ab6-a512-08f4a25455b4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
General Motors is releasing a software update enabling owners of 250,000 bidirectional capable electric vehicles to[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/abe8283d-1ca9-4cf1-9163-46ba5b9b0d64?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[sell electricity from their cars](https://substack.com/redirect/abe8283d-1ca9-4cf1-9163-46ba5b9b0d64?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** back to the U.S. power grid during peak demand.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c7ae32c7-9d19-4ab6-a512-08f4a25455b4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Vehicle to Grid Update:** The change expands vehicle to home capability so EVs can support utilities and earn compensation for owners while GM takes a portion.
* **Massive Storage Potential:** Quarter million vehicles could power 120,000 homes for up to one week during outages.
* **Testing With Utilities:** Pilots underway with Pacific Gas and Electric and DTE Energy using GM employee homes to build reliable backup capacity.
* **Fifty Two Thousand By Thirty Thirty:** Company expects more than 52,000 GM EVs participating in grid balancing protocols nationwide by end of decade.

Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

What motivates much of my work in the Senate today comes down to where my story began. So today, I want to share that story with you - and explain how it informs my why.
I grew up in a working-class family, as the granddaughter of Jewish immigrants and the daughter of a World War II veteran. My loved ones instilled in me the values of hard work, determination, and persistence that I've carried with me my whole life.
_That 's why_ I fight so hard to ensure veterans and hardworking Americans get the hard-earned benefits they deserve.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/729a5480-b422-41d4-a377-23f63ecda861?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
After graduating high school, I worked as a cocktail waitress at Caesars Palace to help pay for college, and I became the first in my family to graduate.
_That 's why_ I fight so hard to improve public education and increase opportunities for young people.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/729a5480-b422-41d4-a377-23f63ecda861?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I became the third Jewish woman and only former synagogue president ever elected to the U.S. Senate. To this day, my work is guided by the principle of "tikkun olam" - which means to repair the world and leave it in a better place than we found it.
_That 's why_ I fight so hard in the Senate to make progress and positive change for all the people in our country.
**I will never stop fighting for a better future for you and your loved ones because** _**that 's why **_**I got into politics.**
But right now, Washington Republicans control the Senate majority. And what _they_ are fighting for is this: Greenlighting Trump's entire destructive agenda.
Now, hardworking Americans are paying the price as vital programs like SNAP, Medicaid, Medicare, WIC, and other critical benefits are cut. Meanwhile, Trump's tariffs, military actions, and other reckless policies are making everything less affordable.
Instead of working to fix the damage they've caused, Trump and his Republican allies in the Senate are trying to restrict access to the ballot box to stop people from holding them accountable this November.
I'm working with Democrats to pick up the pieces and protect our rights in any way we can. But to actually go back to making real progress for everyday Americans, we need to take back our Senate majority.
_**That 's why **_**I 'm so grateful for grassroots supporters like you on my team who are so crucial in our fight to flip the Senate blue.**
Together, I know we will be able to hold Republicans accountable in the midterms, limit Trump's damage in the second half of his term, and leave our country in a better place than it is now.
Thank you for standing with me.
- Jacky

Michigan is now a central battleground in the war over the U.S. relationship with Israel--and the American public's ability to debate it freely.

_Story by Tom Perkins and Ryan Grim_
DETROIT, Michigan--Slowly at first, and now all at once, Michigan has turned into the central battleground in the country's war over the U.S. relationship with Israel--and the American public's ability to debate it freely.
Campuses across the country erupted in protest in 2024 against U.S. complicity in Israel's ongoing genocide, with crackdowns of various intensity rolling up encampments, disciplining students, and, in some cases, filing significant charges.
Michigan's law enforcement moved perhaps the most aggressively. When a local prosecutor in Ann Arbor declined to press felony charges on a group of protest organizers, state Attorney General Dana Nessel moved to take matters into her own hands. Now that those charges have been met with acquittals and dismissals, the federal government is stepping in to target them with felonies, announcing a sweeping indictment filed Wednesday against eight pro-Palestinian advocates.

Along the way, protesters organized against the University of Michigan Regents who pushed for the charges. Jordan Acker, one of the most vitriolic advocates of criminalizing protest against Israel, was replaced by Lebanese American Amir Makled, who campaigned against the crackdown on protest. Then in the race for attorney general, Eli Savit--the very Ann Arbor prosecutor who refused to press charges on the protesters--won the Democratic Party's nomination.
In the campaign for Senate, despite millions in outside spending from AIPAC, Dr. Abdul El-Sayed recently broke out as the frontrunner for the party's nomination once the race began to focus on the question of American support for Israel. That primary is in August.
Across the board, voters in Michigan are loudly demanding a change in the relationship. At the heights of power, state and federal leaders are pulling every lever to thwart that democratic will. In the Michigan legislature, state lawmakers have responded to the shock upset in the Board of Regents election by proposing to end elections for the Board of Regents. The constitutional amendments were voted down, but a new proposal is expected to come up in August.
The three-pronged approach to suppressing dissent in Michigan--spending millions in the Senate primary, ending Regent elections, and criminalizing protest at the federal level--marks a dramatic escalation in the government's crackdown on criticism of Israel.
The University of Michigan-affiliated protesters are accused of vandalizing the homes of the school's leadership and targeting international businesses, like Rolls-Royce and shipping giant Maersk. But federal prosecutors with the Trump Department of Justice organized crime unit went much further than vandalism charges.
The indictment claims that regular activist activities--like using social media or "buying supplies"--amount to a broad "conspiracy" and "coordinated criminal acts." Those activities ultimately aimed to threaten U-M leadership and foreign businesses over their support of Israel, the indictment claims, forming the basis for multiple counts of "conspiring to transmit threats in interstate and foreign commerce."
The charges represent a change in tack from recent pro-Israel legal lawsuits and prosecutions alleging hate crimes or antisemitism. Courts have regularly struck down those, ruling that criticism of Israel is First Amendment-protected speech.
But the government did have success with effectively--and controversially--criminalizing activism in the Prairieland, Texas ICE protest case, in which the Trump administration accused activists of materially supporting terrorism in part because they had anarchist zines. The first Trump administration also tried to use similar tactics against 2017 inauguration protesters, and they have been wielded against animal rights activists.
Experts say they are not surprised the conspiracy charges are now being tested at the University of Michigan. In a statement, Arab-American Civil Rights League director Houda Berri-Harajli said that while vandalism should be investigated, the actions by University of Michigan, Nessel, and Trump represent "overreach" aimed at silencing pro-Palestinian advocates. "The concern is whether the government is increasingly using broad conspiracy theories, political speech, social media posts, and activism itself as evidence to build cases against individuals associated with a movement that has become politically unpopular in certain circles," Berri-Harajli said.
## **The Charges**
The protesters are largely members of the U-M's TAHRIR Coalition and Students Allied for Freedom and Equality (SAFE), a Students for Justice in Palestine chapter. Their campaign was aimed at pressuring U-M and businesses to divest from, or stop doing business with, Israel.
The eight defendants are accused of vandalizing the homes of former U-M President Santa Ono, U-M regents, and multiple businesses. The indictment states that the protesters spraypainted "pro-Palestinian" or "anti-Israel graffiti" on homes and businesses, and broke glass at some. In one instance, they allegedly threw a bottle of butyric acid, also known as a "stink bomb," into a home, and allegedly padlocked or caulked shut the doors of certain businesses.
The DOJ lays the foundation for the "conspiracy" with statements that largely detail common activism activities. "[Protesters] planning efforts included purchasing supplies, meeting to coordinate and distribute supplies, mapping routes, performing surveillance, and using internet-based collaboration tools to draft threats to their targets," the indictment states.
It further claims the defendants "used the internet" to research "targets," who are largely public officials. It continues that protesters used "the internet and social media to broadcast their message to ensure their threats and commitment to continuing criminal activity were heard by their victims and others who support Israel."
The prosecutors are attempting to create a "myth of criminality" in activism, said Liz Jacobs, an attorney for the protesters with Sugar Law Center.
Federal prosecutors allege the "threats" were made in slogans spraypainted on the homes and businesses, including "Intifada" and "Divest now." The government also claims protesters used "threatening symbols" like red inverted triangles. Courts [have ruled that these slogans and symbols are protected speech](https://substack.com/redirect/e2ecaa5c-4815-4d19-a67c-03ffb1fcc3a2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in most contexts.
The indictment also points to a note taped to the front door of one home: "No matter how many times you call on violent cops to brutalize students, cancel and move your meetings to hide from students, and refuse to admit this university's and YOUR complicity in genocide, we will continue to protest. You cannot hide. We demand divestment and will remain relentless in the struggle for a free Palestine."
The threat claims are "very loose," said Chip Gibbons, policy director at Defending Rights and Dissent. "They are attempting to transform political speech that is undeniably protected by the First Amendment into overt acts of conspiracy," he added. "It would be a struggle to see these as threats."
The indictment includes one example of an alleged text exchange among two defendants in which they state that they want to "poison" one of the targets, or "burn down" a house. No such actions were ever taken, and those threats were never made to the regents or other alleged victims.
While the vandalism is illegal, the government is ultimately trying "to take something that is a low-level offense at best and ratchet it way up because of the political speech of the alleged perpetrator," Gibbons said. "The FBI, the National Security Agency driven by intelligence--they're not supposed to be spending a lot of time on who is spray painting houses," Gibbons added.

## **" A conscious choice by Nessel"**
The indictment and escalation come amid a series of U-M-Nessel failures in its war on pro-Palestinian protesters, advocates say. "There is a popular movement across Michigan in support of Palestine, human rights, and disinvestment in Israel and the genocide," Jacobs said. "Why keep running the same playbook?"
In May 2024, U-M dispatched police to [violently break up](https://substack.com/redirect/8be327e8-3a55-4fbd-95f2-fcb710bf25a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a Palestinian solidarity encampment, but progressive Ann Arbor prosecutor Eli Savit declined to charge the students. The university then [recruited Nessel, a pro-Israel political ally](https://substack.com/redirect/3e524aef-3088-4559-bb91-540bc8681f4a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), to take over the investigation.
She filed dozens of encampment-related charges in late 2024, but dropped [the cases](https://substack.com/redirect/0b2b8b8e-6e73-4bc0-9dd1-c02a9e71d3c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) after her political, personal, and financial connections to pro-Israel donors and the school's regents were revealed.
Nessel has repeatedly praised herself for "stepping up to the plate" to take on Trump's assault on Michiganders' civil liberties, but in April 2025, she and Trump's FBI opened up a second front, raiding the homes of a new set of protesters over the alleged vandalism.
On Wednesday morning, Nessel's agents and the FBI again raided students' homes, using flash bangs and battering rams in the dramatic arrests.
"That was a conscious choice by Nessel to bring in the Trump administration," Jacobs said.
Amid all of this, the university has fired or suspended pro-Palestinian students and faculty, and spent millions of dollars on undercover surveillance of TAHRIR. Protesters have filed countersuits that judges have largely allowed to move forward.
Wednesday's federal indictment is "consistent with a pattern of escalation and repression that we've been seeing unfolding over the last 2-3 years that's unprecedented and frightening," Eman Ali, a TAHRIR organizer, said outside the courthouse where supporters gathered on Wednesday afternoon.
## **Electoral Consequences**
The draconian assault on protesters is having consequences for the political establishment. In the April Democratic primary nominating convention, TAHRIR attorney Amir Makled defeated pro-Israel U-M regent Jordan Acker, who led the attack on pro-Palestinian students.
In the attorney general race to replace Nessel, voters chose Savit, the progressive prosecutor. He beat a candidate backed by the pro-Israel establishment, and would likely end the Nessel investigations if he wins in November, though the Department of Justice likely would not.
The wins [ignited establishment calls](https://substack.com/redirect/460d77f5-8c7d-4acb-848b-d9eb5c6a3495?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for a change to how state leaders are selected, and Democratic and GOP leaders responded last week by attempting to carry out what critics labeled a "power grab." Currently, Michigan's university board positions, the attorney general, and the secretary of state are voted on by delegates at party conventions.
Constitutional amendments that failed last week either aimed to undo Makled's election or make university regents gubernatorial appointees. A proposal is expected to be reintroduced when lawmakers reconvene in August.
The constitutional amendment proposals are being pushed "because [the establishment] believes it will help them grab more power," said Democrat State Rep. Dylan Wegela, a Democratic Socialist of America member who opposes both proposals.
"They're doing this because progressives won at the convention," Wegela said. "They're doing this to strip voters' ability to pick regents."

But the government did have success with effectively--and controversially--criminalizing activism in the Prairieland, Texas ICE protest case, in which the Trump administration accused activists of materially supporting terrorism in part because they had anarchist zines. The first Trump administration also tried to use similar tactics against 2017 inauguration protesters, and they have been wielded against animal rights activists. Experts say they are not surprised the conspiracy charges are now being tested at the University of Michigan. In a statement, Arab-American Civil Rights League director Houda Berri-Harajli said that while vandalism should be investigated, the actions by University of Michigan, Nessel, and Trump represent "overreach" aimed at silencing pro-Palestinian advocates. "The concern is whether the government is increasingly using broad conspiracy theories, political speech, social media posts, and activism itself as evidence to build cases against individuals associated with a movement that has become politically unpopular in certain circles," Berri-Harajli said. The Charges The protesters are largely members of the U-M's TAHRIR Coalition and Students Allied for Freedom and Equality (SAFE), a Students for Justice in Palestine chapter. Their campaign was aimed at pressuring U-M and businesses to divest from, or stop doing business with, Israel. The eight defendants are accused of vandalizing the homes of former U-M President Santa Ono, U-M regents, and multiple businesses. The indictment states that the protesters spraypainted "pro-Palestinian" or "anti-Israel graffiti" on homes and businesses, and broke glass at some. In one instance, they allegedly threw a bottle of butyric acid, also known as a "stink bomb," into a home, and allegedly padlocked or caulked shut the doors of certain businesses. The DOJ lays the foundation for the "conspiracy" with statements that largely detail common activism activities. "[Protesters] planning efforts included purchasing supplies, meeting to coordinate and distribute supplies, mapping routes, performing surveillance, and using internet-based collaboration tools to draft threats to their targets," the indictment states. It further claims the defendants "used the internet" to research "targets," who are largely public officials. It continues that protesters used "the internet and social media to broadcast their message to ensure their threats and commitment to continuing criminal activity were heard by their victims and others who support Israel." The prosecutors are attempting to create a "myth of criminality" in activism, said Liz Jacobs, an attorney for the protesters with Sugar Law Center. Federal prosecutors allege the "threats" were made in slogans spraypainted on the homes and businesses, including "Intifada" and "Divest now." The government also claims protesters used "threatening symbols" like red inverted triangles. Courts in most contexts. The indictment also points to a note taped to the front door of one home: "No matter how many times you call on violent cops to brutalize students, cancel and move your meetings to hide from students, and refuse to admit this university's and YOUR complicity in genocide, we will continue to protest. You cannot hide. We demand divestment and will remain relentless in the struggle for a free Palestine." The threat claims are "very loose," said Chip Gibbons, policy director at Defending Rights and Dissent. "They are attempting to transform political speech that is undeniably protected by the First Amendment into overt acts of conspiracy," he added. "It would be a struggle to see these as threats." The indictment includes one example of an alleged text exchange among two defendants in which they state that they want to "poison" one of the targets, or "burn down" a house. No such actions were ever taken, and those threats were never made to the regents or other alleged victims. While the vandalism is illegal, the government is ultimately trying "to take something that is a low-level offense at best and ratchet it way up because of the political speech of the alleged perpetrator," Gibbons said. "The FBI, the National Security Agency driven by intelligence--they're not supposed to be spending a lot of time on who is spray painting houses," Gibbons added. Drop Site News is reader-supported. Consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. " A conscious choice by Nessel" The indictment and escalation come amid a series of U-M-Nessel failures in its war on pro-Palestinian protesters, advocates say. "There is a popular movement across Michigan in support of Palestine, human rights, and disinvestment in Israel and the genocide," Jacobs said. "Why keep running the same playbook?" In May 2024, U-M dispatched police to a Palestinian solidarity encampment, but progressive Ann Arbor prosecutor Eli Savit declined to charge the students. The university then , to take over the investigation. She filed dozens of encampment-related charges in late 2024, but dropped after her political, personal, and financial connections to pro-Israel donors and the school's regents were revealed. Nessel has repeatedly praised herself for "stepping up to the plate" to take on Trump's assault on Michiganders' civil liberties, but in April 2025, she and Trump's FBI opened up a second front, raiding the homes of a new set of protesters over the alleged vandalism. On Wednesday morning, Nessel's agents and the FBI again raided students' homes, using flash bangs and battering rams in the dramatic arrests. "That was a conscious choice by Nessel to bring in the Trump administration," Jacobs said. Amid all of this, the university has fired or suspended pro-Palestinian students and faculty, and spent millions of dollars on undercover surveillance of TAHRIR. Protesters have filed countersuits that judges have largely allowed to move forward. Wednesday's federal indictment is "consistent with a pattern of escalation and repression that we've been seeing unfolding over the last 2-3 years that's unprecedented and frightening," Eman Ali, a TAHRIR organizer, said outside the courthouse where supporters gathered on Wednesday afternoon. Electoral Consequences The draconian assault on protesters is having consequences for the political establishment. In the April Democratic primary nominating convention, TAHRIR attorney Amir Makled defeated pro-Israel U-M regent Jordan Acker, who led the attack on pro-Palestinian students. In the attorney general race to replace Nessel, voters chose Savit, the progressive prosecutor. He beat a candidate backed by the pro-Israel establishment, and would likely end the Nessel investigations if he wins in November, though the Department of Justice likely would not. The wins for a change to how state leaders are selected, and Democratic and GOP leaders responded last week by attempting to carry out what critics labeled a "power grab." Currently, Michigan's university board positions, the attorney general, and the secretary of state are voted on by delegates at party conventions. Constitutional amendments that failed last week either aimed to undo Makled's election or make university regents gubernatorial appointees. A proposal is expected to be reintroduced when lawmakers reconvene in August. The constitutional amendment proposals are being pushed "because [the establishment] believes it will help them grab more power," said Democrat State Rep. Dylan Wegela, a Democratic Socialist of America member who opposes both proposals. "They're doing this because progressives won at the convention," Wegela said. California famously takes a long time to count ballots due to the nature of its open primaries, and some candidates faded in the results as more ballots were counted.

body:
From City Hall to Capitol Hill, a quick overview of who is responsible for what.
| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133220949/627125091/-1405467182?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MTY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2ZDE0ZTViMC04YTY2LWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=KYJFWXHSOT-xMB5r5p4qdGbD-iU61Cu9doYRf3Gb8KE=&emci=78494660-8166-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&emdi=6d14e5b0-8a66-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&ceid=14565883)
---

| | Welcome back to Fact Friday. **Today, I want to talk about something that comes up often whenever our community is debating an important local issue: who is actually responsible for making certain decisions?** Unless you're dealing with it every day, it's entirely normal to feel a bit rusty or get confused by the bureaucracy. When an issue affects your neighborhood, your family, or your daily life, it's natural to reach out to the elected officials you know and trust. But knowing _who_ actually holds authority is essential if we want to advocate effectively. **As your representative in Congress, my job is to advocate for El Paso in Washington.** My day-to-day focus centers on federal funding, immigration policy, veterans' services, military installations, major transportation investments, and national legislation affecting healthcare programs like Medicare. Through my seat on the House Appropriations Committee, I help determine how federal resources are invested across the country and work to bring those resources back home. That includes securing funding for projects that strengthen our region, such as investments in cancer care at Texas Tech El Paso and efforts to modernize our land ports of entry. **Knowing where authority rests is just as important as knowing the issue itself.** Local governments have authority over zoning, land use, municipal infrastructure, local ordinances, and decisions about how a city grows and develops. For example, when a neighborhood plot is rezoned for a new apartment building or commercial complex, or when decisions are made about local tax incentives and street repairs, those approvals are handled through local municipal processes and decided by our local elected officials. None of this means federal and local issues are completely isolated from one another. When major local projects arise, I can fight for federal resources, push for transparency, ensure federal regulations protect consumers and taxpayers, and work alongside local leaders to safeguard El Paso's interests. But the authority to approve, reject, or manage many local development decisions ultimately rests with local government. **I believe one of the most important things an elected official can do is be completely honest about what they can and cannot control.** Our system works best when people are empowered with the knowledge about who is responsible for what and know where to direct their advocacy. My commitment to you remains unchanged: to fight for El Paso in Washington and make sure our community's voice is heard at the federal level. If you want to keep getting clear, fact-based breakdowns of the issues affecting our community, make sure you stay connected and share this with someone who should be paying attention, too. Staying informed is power. Let's use it, El Paso. clean_body: From City Hall to Capitol Hill, a quick overview of who is responsible for what. | | | | Welcome back to Fact Friday. Today, I want to talk about something that comes up often whenever our community is debating an important local issue: who is actually responsible for making certain decisions? Unless you're dealing with it every day, it's entirely normal to feel a bit rusty or get confused by the bureaucracy. When an issue affects your neighborhood, your family, or your daily life, it's natural to reach out to the elected officials you know and trust. But knowing who actually holds authority is essential if we want to advocate effectively. As your representative in Congress, my job is to advocate for El Paso in Washington. My day-to-day focus centers on federal funding, immigration policy, veterans' services, military installations, major transportation investments, and national legislation affecting healthcare programs like Medicare. Through my seat on the House Appropriations Committee, I help determine how federal resources are invested across the country and work to bring those resources back home. That includes securing funding for projects that strengthen our region, such as investments in cancer care at Texas Tech El Paso and efforts to modernize our land ports of entry. Knowing where authority rests is just as important as knowing the issue itself. Local governments have authority over zoning, land use, municipal infrastructure, local ordinances, and decisions about how a city grows and develops. For example, when a neighborhood plot is rezoned for a new apartment building or commercial complex, or when decisions are made about local tax incentives and street repairs, those approvals are handled through local municipal processes and decided by our local elected officials. None of this means federal and local issues are completely isolated from one another. When major local projects arise, I can fight for federal resources, push for transparency, ensure federal regulations protect consumers and taxpayers, and work alongside local leaders to safeguard El Paso's interests. But the authority to approve, reject, or manage many local development decisions ultimately rests with local government. I believe one of the most important things an elected official can do is be completely honest about what they can and cannot control. Our system works best when people are empowered with the knowledge about who is responsible for what and know where to direct their advocacy. My commitment to you remains unchanged: to fight for El Paso in Washington and make sure our community's voice is heard at the federal level. If you want to keep getting clear, fact-based breakdowns of the issues affecting our community, make sure you stay connected and share this with someone who should be paying attention, too. Staying informed is power. Let's use it, El Paso. These boxes aren't sitting around waiting for someone to need them.

They're already claimed. And we don't have extras.

By the time one batch goes out, more requests come in.

Different schools, different students, same situation -- they want to start something, and they're asking us to help them do it.

That's where things stand right now.

We have more students stepping up than we can fully support at the moment.

And I don't say that lightly.

Because for years, the challenge wasn't getting students the tools -- it was getting them to speak up at all. Most kept their heads down.

The Left has spent years trying to convince this generation to sit down, stay quiet, and be ashamed of their country and everything that makes it great.

And for a long time, it worked. But that's all changing.

Now, we're seeing students stand up and push back.

**We saw it clearly at Wheeling High School in the Chicago suburbs -- Charlie's alma mater. **

For the first time, students there launched a Club America chapter. It took months to get approved, but a chapter is finally there.

And now, students are standing outside with signs about free markets and freedom -- not because it's easy, but because they've decided it matters more than staying quiet.

That's not something you can just manufacture. But it is something you can support when it happens.

And it's not isolated growth anymore.

**We 're now working with more than 1,450 college chapters and over 3,400 high school chapters across the country. That's real scale. **

But if you zoom out, there are roughly 27,000 high schools in America.

That means tens of thousands of campuses where the Left still dominates the conversation...

And where students are waiting for someone to help them stand up and speak.

So as much as this has grown, we're still in the early innings of what Charlie actually set out to build.

What's different now is the pace.

**Many states are moving to bring Club America chapters to every high school statewide, including: **

✅ Arkansas
✅ Florida
✅ Idaho
✅ Indiana
✅ Montana
✅ Nebraska
✅ Oklahoma
✅ South Carolina
✅ Texas
✅ Tennessee

That brings us to ten states now taking this seriously -- not just talk, but action.

That kind of expansion doesn't happen slowly.

It stacks quickly -- and it creates pressure behind the scenes to keep up.

Because every new chapter, every new student leader, every new school means more materials, more support, more follow-through.

And right now, that's where we're stretched.

We're not lacking interest or momentum.

We're working to keep up with both.

_So here 's how you can help... _

Right now, there are students ready to step up -- they just need the tools to do it.

**An activism kit puts everything they need directly into their hands: **

✅ Constitutions.
✅ Chapter guides.
✅ Flags.
✅ Materials to organize and lead.

It turns a student who wants to speak up... _into one who actually does. _

And you'll make it possible for us to keep saying yes when a student reaches out and says, "I want to start something here."

clean_body: I wanted you to see this I want to give you a picture of what's really happening right now -- not the polished version, but what it actually looks like on the ground. | | | | | Patriot, I want to give you a picture of what's really happening right now -- not the polished version, but what it actually looks like on the ground. Inside our office, tables are covered in supplies and open boxes. Coworkers are coming together, packing materials, sealing kits, and sending them out the door as fast as possible. Above: Activism kits bound for new chapters being packed with Constitutions, chapter handbooks, American flags, and more at TPUSA HQ in Arizona These boxes aren't sitting around waiting for someone to need them. They're already claimed. And we don't have extras. By the time one batch goes out, more requests come in. Different schools, different students, same situation -- they want to start something, and they're asking us to help them do it. That's where things stand right now. We have more students stepping up than we can fully support at the moment. And I don't say that lightly. Because for years, the challenge wasn't getting students the tools -- it was getting them to speak up at all. Most kept their heads down. The Left has spent years trying to convince this generation to sit down, stay quiet, and be ashamed of their country and everything that makes it great. And for a long time, it worked. But that's all changing. Now, we're seeing students stand up and push back. We saw it clearly at Wheeling High School in the Chicago suburbs -- Charlie's alma mater. For the first time, students there launched a Club America chapter. It took months to get approved, but a chapter is finally there. And now, students are standing outside with signs about free markets and freedom -- not because it's easy, but because they've decided it matters more than staying quiet. That's not something you can just manufacture. But it is something you can support when it happens. And it's not isolated growth anymore. We 're now working with more than 1,450 college chapters and over 3,400 high school chapters across the country. That's real scale. But if you zoom out, there are roughly 27,000 high schools in America. That means tens of thousands of campuses where the Left still dominates the conversation... And where students are waiting for someone to help them stand up and speak. So as much as this has grown, we're still in the early innings of what Charlie actually set out to build. What's different now is the pace. Many states are moving to bring Club America chapters to every high school statewide, including: ✅ Arkansas ✅ Florida ✅ Idaho ✅ Indiana ✅ Montana ✅ Nebraska ✅ Oklahoma ✅ South Carolina ✅ Texas ✅ Tennessee That brings us to ten states now taking this seriously -- not just talk, but action. That kind of expansion doesn't happen slowly. It stacks quickly -- and it creates pressure behind the scenes to keep up. Because every new chapter, every new student leader, every new school means more materials, more support, more follow-through. And right now, that's where we're stretched. We're not lacking interest or momentum. We're working to keep up with both. So here 's how you can help... Right now, there are students ready to step up -- they just need the tools to do it. An activism kit puts everything they need directly into their hands: ✅ Constitutions. ✅ Chapter guides. ✅ Flags. ✅ Materials to organize and lead. It turns a student who wants to speak up... into one who actually does. And you'll make it possible for us to keep saying yes when a student reaches out and says, "I want to start something here." Every activism kit you help sponsor means one more student is ready to lead instead of sitting on the sidelines. That's how we keep saying "yes" when the next student steps forward. That's how this movement actually scales. Because the reality is, the demand is here now. The only question is whether we're equipped to meet it. And that comes down to whether people like you decide to step in and help carry this forward. One final thing: I also wanted to say thank you. If you've supported Turning Point USA before -- whether once or many times -- you've already played a role in building what you're seeing right now. Students finding their voice. More state partnerships. New TPUSA chapters like the one at Charlie's former high school. This kind of momentum doesn't happen without people willing to stand behind it. Washington loves a headline. A cable news hit. A tweet that trends for 24 hours and disappears by morning.
You know what Washington doesn't love? **Showing up.**
Scott DesJarlais hasn't truly shown up for this district in years. He's shown up for donor dinners. He's shown up for party votes. He's shown up when the cameras were pointed in his direction and the right people were watching. But when it came to sitting across from a grandmother worried about her prescription costs, or a small business owner who hasn't taken a day off in two years and still can't get ahead... **he was nowhere to be found.**
We are doing this differently. Completely. Unapologetically. **And we need your help to keep it up in the face of GOP funding and Big PAC money![🔵CLICK HERE!🔵](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/d50d1be9-144d-4512-a49e-d8bae0d059a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

---|---|---
[PITCH IN $20.26 TO WIN 2026!](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/d50d1be9-144d-4512-a49e-d8bae0d059a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
We've been across three counties. We've hired 20 interns. We've attended community events that will never make the news because that's not why we were there. We were there because the people of Tennessee's 4th District deserve a candidate who treats them like the entire point of the campaign, not the backdrop for it.
That's not just a different style, It's a direct rejection of everything DesJarlais has stood for in this seat for 14 years. A rejection of the transactional, donor-first, constituent-last brand of politics that has left working families in this district without a real voice in Washington for over a decade.
**Hometowns over headlines. That 's the campaign. That's the promise. That's what wins this year, because it is what Americans deserve.**

---
| | | Dear Peter,
---
It’s dusty, with a hint of woodsmoke and a sharp, resinous note of pine boughs. A Sonoma County sauvignon blanc? Nope—just your camping gear, stashed away since last summer’s final campout.
---
If you’ve been missing the glow of a campfire and the sticky sweetness of s’mores, you’re not alone. We’re already poring over maps, dreaming up summer adventures. There’s nothing like a night in the redwoods—the outside world hushed, the forest close, stars drifting overhead. It’s a feeling worth protecting. Your support sustains not just trees and wildlife, but places to recharge, reflect, and connect with the redwoods. That generosity keeps these special spaces alive, now and into the future. Ready to head out? Start with these guides to some of our favorite overnight experiences in the redwoods.

A Sonoma County sauvignon blanc? Nope—just your camping gear, stashed away since last summer’s final campout. If you’ve been missing the glow of a campfire and the sticky sweetness of s’mores, you’re not alone. We’re already poring over maps, dreaming up summer adventures. There’s nothing like a night in the redwoods—the outside world hushed, the forest close, stars drifting overhead. It’s a feeling worth protecting. Your support sustains not just trees and wildlife, but places to recharge, reflect, and connect with the redwoods. That generosity keeps these special spaces alive, now and into the future. Ready to head out? Start with these guides to some of our favorite overnight experiences in the redwoods. If you’re headed to the North Coast: From fern-lined canyons to oceanfront bluffs, showcase the best of Redwood National and State Parks. If you’re near San Francisco: Explore —Henry Cowell, Portola Redwoods, and Samuel P. Taylor. Each offers scenic campsites and easy access to trails. subject: Protecting the Right to Contraception
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ELIZABETH PANNILL FLETCHER FOR CONGRESS
body:
ELIZABETH PANNILL FLETCHER FOR CONGRESS [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/82676/images/Non-Re-Elect%20Logo.png]
This week marks the anniversary of Griswold v. Connecticut , the landmark Supreme Court decision of 1960 that recognized the right of married couples to use birth control.
For decades, that decision helped establish a fundamental principle: that deeply personal decisions about our health, our families, and our futures belong to us—not the government.
Today, that principle is under attack.
Since the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade , we have seen efforts to roll back reproductive rights across the country, including attempts to restrict access to contraception. And while the vast majority of Americans support access to birth control, many Republican-controlled legislatures and right-wing organizations are aggressively pushing policies that would put the right and the ability to access birth control at risk.
That is why last year I filed the Right to Contraception Act , a bill to protect access to safe, effective, FDA-approved birth control for people across our country. And it’s why this week, I filed a discharge petition to force the House of Representatives to vote on it. 198 Members of Congress have already signed the discharge petition.
Will you add your name to our citizens petition to show your support for protecting the right to contraception and urge Congress to take action? [https://secure.ngpvan.com/EbxqKXpP90Wrn4hewdEIVQ2]
ADD YOUR SUPPORT [https://secure.ngpvan.com/EbxqKXpP90Wrn4hewdEIVQ2]
Efforts to restrict access to birth control are not about reflecting the will of the American people. They are about taking away the freedom, privacy, dignity, and autonomy that Americans deserve.
As a representative from Texas—a state where reproductive rights have been under relentless attack—I will continue working with my colleagues in Congress to protect and restore the rights and freedoms that women and families depend on. We cannot afford to take these rights for granted, and we cannot give up.
Defending our freedoms requires all of us to stay engaged, organized, and committed to the work ahead.
If you agree that every American should have the freedom to access contraception and make their own health care decisions, please add your name today. [https://secure.ngpvan.com/EbxqKXpP90Wrn4hewdEIVQ2]
ADD YOUR SUPPORT [https://secure.ngpvan.com/EbxqKXpP90Wrn4hewdEIVQ2]
Thank you for standing with me in this fight.

clean_body: ELIZABETH PANNILL FLETCHER FOR CONGRESS [] This week marks the anniversary of Griswold v. Connecticut , the landmark Supreme Court decision of 1960 that recognized the right of married couples to use birth control. For decades, that decision helped establish a fundamental principle: that deeply personal decisions about our health, our families, and our futures belong to us—not the government. Today, that principle is under attack. Since the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade , we have seen efforts to roll back reproductive rights across the country, including attempts to restrict access to contraception. And while the vast majority of Americans support access to birth control, many Republican-controlled legislatures and right-wing organizations are aggressively pushing policies that would put the right and the ability to access birth control at risk. That is why last year I filed the Right to Contraception Act , a bill to protect access to safe, effective, FDA-approved birth control for people across our country. And it’s why this week, I filed a discharge petition to force the House of Representatives to vote on it. 198 Members of Congress have already signed the discharge petition. Will you add your name to our citizens petition to show your support for protecting the right to contraception and urge Congress to take action? body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
I want to tell you something that’s not easy to talk about...
A sitting Republican elected official recently tagged the Department of Homeland Security on social media and wrote: "I would like to report a foreign occupier. Name: Unpronounceable. Country of origin: Tatooine." He was talking about me. The same official called for the mass deportation of Indian Americans.
I was born in New Delhi. I came to this country as a baby. I grew up in Peoria, Illinois. I went to public schools, got on food stamps for a time with my family, worked my way to Princeton and Harvard Law. I served in government. I got elected to Congress four times.
And someone still looked at all of that and saw a foreign occupier.
I'm telling you this not for sympathy. I'm telling you this because what happened to me is happening to communities all across this country right now, at a scale we have never seen before.
Trump and his MAGA allies have made it clear: if you weren't born here, if your name is hard to pronounce, if you look different or pray differently, you are not fully American in their eyes. They are using the machinery of the federal government to make that point, loudly and cruelly, every single day.
My father came here with nothing. He believed this country would be there for families like ours. It was. Barely. Because people fought for it.
That is exactly why I started Equal Opportunity Now.
We need leaders in office who will stand up for immigrant families and for every community that Trump has decided to make an enemy.
Those leaders exist. They are running for office right now. They need our support.
Will you chip in $25 or $50 today to help Equal Opportunity Now back the leaders who won't back down? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
DONATE NOW! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
It’s on us to stop the rising tide of MAGA Extremism. And with your help? We’ll be unstoppable.
— Raja Krishnamoorthi
Founder, Equal Opportunity Now
Visit Our Website To Learn More! [https://www.equalopportunitynow.org/]

Fellow Conservative,

**I just won the Minnesota GOP endorsement for the U.S. Senate — but I’m not celebrating. **

Because while we were earning the trust of Republican delegates in Duluth, the radical left was doubling down on the same insanity that’s destroying our state.

_**Take a look at this:**_

_[](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=b0de581bac57406c83dfe964b6708c90&_e=Nxr3tl_qOvD_dCMnXSVeVDTaV5ZPo08_bWIfSJuDd6p3aMXL2tmhFtOvkAVXibnA4z485E64ivPbFo1zGYEQRsqz0TGbApMUW0jC_uAmnCYCbCuJWqM_GG7o8LeVqEhJ9B78BWejJFD-FwCxOMy5ugwa_QQnpBANqUYkO0kcGACvLSf9g8NI61BI9fvMELQN355u3OJinSm1_C9zaQDMPRXfVApXChphnPwa_TrDn2_s6PE0EsPf9l0Ew4JKFGoDk3o_cYRHzP_iVFfJEq0o0yliVsMfwNb7oMBA5eMW3oG-zl6MhrfRlTKUVDc-yKPFyET_10yPYenVVvd2WSDYqVuQU-T87rF7mmCDc9_jcZTwZ75c-IptKhPJNgMbhWdR6V1MfAOX5nwqdHKmD6Loxu5Qr8_I5hcYCeW2yVyDnvn-J01KhwtyDyXzKcbzNmvLWmEa0iksgiJcENomIAgnRTrAgrYR4PMRrzpGScaCO-BpTu_jckutScKW_Bg0x-a4X_BwzhcKknKBVylhlUJg1LRQn21ToVteehPSmwspylGYxNFuu7kUcSAiXdhBdTafmM9C9Nv5ymLeuEgmE-QjyeLduyNaHA3SS9p_Tsx8xlPCRSx18B0_FV1UOj9lsE6fsO4mkHF6sEZMgHuqxLvAAUR4HpUp7gg5EEzkJJXWOoVDNHNYfrr5psxNRKqc7JxpXsAOdATxByCaX9C6KXn-HPdVhEu9bmrhbosBYJdqhZnZA4Zp9zFVJIAj5Sfd0GdG)_
This is Lieutenant Governor Peggy Flanagan — Tim Walz’s **insane 2nd-in-command** , and the person standing between Minnesota and real leadership in the U.S. Senate.

_**She’s been cosplaying as a Somali Muslim.**_****

This isn’t leadership. It’s cynical cultural appropriation — the same tired game we’ve seen from the far left for years. And it shows exactly how out of touch these radicals have become with real Minnesotans.
981925
As we approach America’s 250th anniversary, I keep asking myself:_**Is this the legacy we want to leave our children?**_

**I didn’t enter this fight to play games. On my 18th birthday, weeks after 9/11, I joined the Marine Corps and fought in the Battle of Najaf. I later became a Navy SEAL and deployed nine times across the globe. I’ve seen what happens when leaders put ideology over duty.**

That same sense of duty brought me home to Minnesota._**I watched Tim Walz abandon Minneapolis while riots raged — even near my own sister’s home.**_ I saw our police defunded, our streets burned, and hardworking families crushed under higher taxes and radical policies.

[**STOP THE FAR LEFT AGENDA
**](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=b0de581bac57406c83dfe964b6708c90&_e=Nxr3tl_qOvD_dCMnXSVeVDTaV5ZPo08_bWIfSJuDd6p3aMXL2tmhFtOvkAVXibnA4z485E64ivPbFo1zGYEQRsqz0TGbApMUW0jC_uAmnCYCbCuJWqM_GG7o8LeVqEhJ9B78BWejJFD-FwCxOMy5ugwa_QQnpBANqUYkO0kcGACvLSf9g8NI61BI9fvMELQN355u3OJinSm1_C9zaQDMPRXfVApXChphnPwa_TrDn2_s6PE0EsPf9l0Ew4JKFGoDk3o_cYRHzP_iVFfJEq0o09oLalowH4_c3zlGP5MZ7FLOJj68FMZID52ygtPYlKFLRuVXYYMNPezwXqP0msGqXgMEllRghGyDXYY4t6lnxamNcJn5xX9DwvDnzspNIx--RYrhdd18vkjGsmH2YUu5cRGng7chuSKMd76Ch51K54VS4MwumZrN-VuYYNjMZRGbb-gVT-eiBbn7ll_3hh2OWTaUGs1RADwhjtIcFcxbEMvqh_vV-91ZlmsXx3rYHlq0TwiZJKeARAvy3w9J6U8njBl5MNYwEuRPd6lwIlFuUdPb44GN2zVNqqtFqY0XG_gl2CIXl2zXQHqKtql1SI7PQNbWfNPX7h8VADeYNyoSffpXwhoR9CnTQ93bMreDzjc2JHhNatdkUYRiOemMeeSra45M5zZlC7XS9WPNchPs8DK-anWimDuLO8ykJ8U1WA3z1TqLCJL9wnszKn3sO5Y8eWJYVEIIMd_ITLrdqPZE_kH1jr1WUIPFoQ5v865-UudA)
That’s why I spent the last year grinding across this state — going to local events, listening to real people, and earning the Republican Party’s endorsement the right way.

_**Now the real battle begins.**_

**Peggy Flanagan and the Walz machine represent the worst of the modern Democratic Party:** covering up fraud, open borders, boys in girls’ sports, attacks on law enforcement, and a growing pro-Hamas radicalism that rejects everything our Founding Fathers stood for.

I’m not a career politician. I’m a combat veteran, a Christian, and a proud working-class Minnesotan who still believes in secure borders, safe communities, and the American Dream.

clean_body: The Washington elites just got a loud wake-up call from Minnesota. | Fellow Conservative, I just won the Minnesota GOP endorsement for the U.S. Senate — but I’m not celebrating. Because while we were earning the trust of Republican delegates in Duluth, the radical left was doubling down on the same insanity that’s destroying our state. Take a look at this: This is Lieutenant Governor Peggy Flanagan — Tim Walz’s insane 2nd-in-command , and the person standing between Minnesota and real leadership in the U.S. Senate. She’s been cosplaying as a Somali Muslim.** This isn’t leadership. It’s cynical cultural appropriation — the same tired game we’ve seen from the far left for years. And it shows exactly how out of touch these radicals have become with real Minnesotans. 981925 As we approach America’s 250th anniversary, I keep asking myself:Is this the legacy we want to leave our children? I didn’t enter this fight to play games. On my 18th birthday, weeks after 9/11, I joined the Marine Corps and fought in the Battle of Najaf. I later became a Navy SEAL and deployed nine times across the globe. I’ve seen what happens when leaders put ideology over duty. That same sense of duty brought me home to Minnesota.I watched Tim Walz abandon Minneapolis while riots raged — even near my own sister’s home. I saw our police defunded, our streets burned, and hardworking families crushed under higher taxes and radical policies. That’s why I spent the last year grinding across this state — going to local events, listening to real people, and earning the Republican Party’s endorsement the right way. Now the real battle begins. Peggy Flanagan and the Walz machine represent the worst of the modern Democratic Party: covering up fraud, open borders, boys in girls’ sports, attacks on law enforcement, and a growing pro-Hamas radicalism that rejects everything our Founding Fathers stood for. I’m not a career politician. I’m a combat veteran, a Christian, and a proud working-class Minnesotan who still believes in secure borders, safe communities, and the American Dream. Fellow Conservative, I can’t win this alone. I’m not asking for the kind of sacrifice I made on nine deployments. I’m simply asking you to join the fight as a patriot. body:

| |
# DNC Organizer Bootcamps
---
| |
We’re excited to share a new training opportunity from the Democratic National Committee: the **When We Count Organizer Bootcamps** , a program designed for graduating college seniors and aspiring young professionals seeking their _first_ campaign job as an organizer for the 2026 midterms.**** These train-to-hire bootcamps will train the next generation of organizers and place them in battleground campaigns across the nation.

[Bootcamps will be hosted virtually to maximize impact](https://us.list-manage.com/11gwsJWPbWT?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e), provide accessible options to attendees, and support coordinated campaigns and state parties.
The first **virtual bootcamp is scheduled for June 25 and 26 from 10 a.m. - 5 p.m. ET**.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/m3HuGupoqwu?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e)
| [APPLY HERE](https://us.list-manage.com/2Coq3jPDOR5?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e)
---
| |
Upon the completion of each bootcamp, the DNC will directly share attendees’ resumes with battleground campaigns staffing up for critical roles in the midterms.
We will host a **virtual information session** to answer questions about the Organizer Bootcamps on **June 17 at 3 p.m. ET / 12 p.m. PT.** [Register on Zoom for the session](https://us.list-manage.com/zVHYpGEAB0m?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e).
This is a wonderful opportunity for young people looking to get involved with politics for the first time! **We would love your support in amplifying the program and recruiting applicants.** Thank you for your continued support, and let me know if you have any questions!
---

It’s been over a hundred days since Trump launched this needless war in Iran
# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=2275%2E791427%2EDVmV6S)
**Friend, an urgent ask from Ilhan Omar:_END THIS WAR NOW!_**
It’s now been over a hundred days since Trump launched his needless war with Iran, which has destabilized the region and killed far too many.
**After two months of negotiations, Trump has failed miserably to secure peace, and now the bombings and strikes are starting up again on both sides.**
[**We’re calling on this proudly anti-war movement to join Ilhan Omar as she pushes her colleagues in Congress to step in and stop Trump’s war. Sign on today and help us show an outpouring of grassroots support:**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em_end_iran_war_jun26/?source=em260612-1-180&refcode2=2275.791427.DVmV6S&akid=2275%2E791427%2EDVmV6S)
**[ADD YOUR NAME](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em_end_iran_war_jun26/?source=em260612-1-180&refcode2=2275.791427.DVmV6S&akid=2275%2E791427%2EDVmV6S)**
Friend, Trump started this war without the support of the American people or America’s allies.
That opposition quickly turned out to be correct — Iranian civilians have been killed, US soldiers have been killed, and the entire region has been destabilized for essentially no gain. Americans aren't safer, and Iranians certainly aren’t better off.
Countries like Iraq, Kuwait, Bahrain, and the UAE have been caught in the crossfire simply as a consequence of their allyship with the US under Trump.
Israel has used this war as a reason to attack and invade Lebanon, killing thousands and displacing over a million people from their homes in their ancestral villages and cities. That’s not to mention a sharp spike of settler violence in the West Bank, and an intensified Israeli blockade of Gaza.
And of course, here at home we are experiencing a sharp increase in the cost of gas, and with it the cost of goods, thanks to the standoff in the Strait of Hormuz — another aspect of this war that has been wildly mishandled and miscalculated by Trump.
**Congress has the power to bring this madness to an end before it becomes another Forever War. It’s time to act.**
[**Please, sign on today and tell Congress that it’s past time to pass a War Powers Resolution and bring this war to an end. Help Ilhan do everything she can to rein in Trump and save lives before even more are lost.**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em_end_iran_war_jun26/?source=em260612-1-180&refcode2=2275.791427.DVmV6S&akid=2275%2E791427%2EDVmV6S)

In solidarity,
Team Ilhan

# [Demand Public Release of Trump’s Cognitive Test Results](https://default.salsalabs.org/Tc8454313-6f58-4a55-ab45-70126ad01fe5/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)
_ Already taken this action? [Go here for more](https://default.salsalabs.org/T35901046-e8ed-4593-a6f6-798f197615ff/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9))_ The American people have a right to know whether the person making life-and-death decisions on war, the economy, and public safety is mentally fit to serve. When members of Congress begin openly discussing the 25th Amendment, we are already in dangerous territory. Silence and secrecy from the White House only deepen the crisis. Particularly since the guy seems just plain bonkers. **[Add your name, and demand that Trump's FULL cognitive test results be released](https://default.salsalabs.org/Te758bbc0-29d1-41d6-b70d-3d0e9ebb9c55/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)**[**.**](https://default.salsalabs.org/T51725bf6-f919-464c-8238-b03e2976cdd5/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) This should not be a partisan issue, it should be a “don’t want to die” issue. If you’re in a bus on a narrow mountain road, you’d want to know if your driver dropped acid, and is seeing exit ramps that don’t actually exist. And if you entrust the nuclear launch codes to one guy, you’d want to make sure his brain wasn’t in permanent meltdown mode. Trump likes to brag that he does well on cognitive tests that ask him to spell “cat” and count to 3, and go potty by himself. So let’s see those tests! **[Add your name, and demand that Trump’s FULL cognitive test results be released](https://default.salsalabs.org/T6be85ee1-f9d8-42cf-8355-49a5b80581eb/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)**[**.**](https://default.salsalabs.org/Td4dee7e3-91a1-45c8-a950-72c0d21de02f/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)

| | **During a time when partisanship seems to be the new "normal," I wanted to take a moment to share three bipartisan wins. **Bipartisanship does exist, and first up, I want to talk about the _21st Century ROAD to Housing Act_ : This bill is not a be-all-and-end-all fix to the housing affordability crisis, but it provides real solutions to the barriers in the way of constructing more affordable housing and the challenges that renters face. It would:
* Expand the number of homes, apartment complexes, and other housing options by reducing unnecessary regulatory barriers to new home construction.
* Prevent private equity firms from buying significant numbers of single-family homes.
* Create a renter complaint hotline and resource center for reporting, monitoring and resolving renter disputes with large institutional investor landlords.
* Establish procedures for timely responses by the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) and large institutional landlords and connect renters with State authorities.
* Require annual reporting on renter disputes and annual notification by large institutional landlords to HUD about the number and location of their properties.
* Support community financial institutions that provide critical financing to homebuyers and housing developers.

**The second bipartisan victory is the Ensuring Rural Health Care Access for Military and Tribal Families Act.** As health care costs continue to rise, rural hospitals that provide care for local servicemembers, like Island Health in Anacortes, are struggling to maintain their current operations. This legislation will help more rural hospitals receive Critical Access Hospital designation, creating a cost-saving lifeline that will preserve vital services and ensure quality medical care for servicemembers. I will keep fighting to protect rural hospitals and the communities they serve in Northwest Washington. **The third bipartisan victory is the BUILD America 250 Act.** Every day is Infrastructure Day in Northwest Washington. The BUILD America 250 Act will employ women and men in my district building roads, bridges, highways, transit, culverts and more. You cannot have a big-league economy with little-league infrastructure, and the investments made by the BUILD America 250 Act will upgrade Northwest Washington's infrastructure and upgrade our economy. Support community financial institutions that provide critical financing to homebuyers and housing developers. The second bipartisan victory is the Ensuring Rural Health Care Access for Military and Tribal Families Act. As health care costs continue to rise, rural hospitals that provide care for local servicemembers, like Island Health in Anacortes, are struggling to maintain their current operations. This legislation will help more rural hospitals receive Critical Access Hospital designation, creating a cost-saving lifeline that will preserve vital services and ensure quality medical care for servicemembers. I will keep fighting to protect rural hospitals and the communities they serve in Northwest Washington. The third bipartisan victory is the BUILD America 250 Act. Every day is Infrastructure Day in Northwest Washington. The BUILD America 250 Act will employ women and men in my district building roads, bridges, highways, transit, culverts and more. You cannot have a big-league economy with little-league infrastructure, and the investments made by the BUILD America 250 Act will upgrade Northwest Washington's infrastructure and upgrade our economy. Senator Tom Cotton | | Tom Cotton is a sixth-generation Arkansan born and raised on his family's cattle farm in Yell County. He graduated from Dardanelle High School before earning a bachelor's degree from Harvard University and a J.D. from Harvard Law School. After clerking on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit and briefly practicing law, the September 11 attacks redirected the course of his life. Cotton joined the United States Army as an Infantry Officer and served nearly five years on active duty. He deployed to Iraq with the 101st Airborne Division and to Afghanistan with a Provincial Reconstruction Team. Between those combat tours, he led a platoon with The Old Guard at Arlington National Cemetery — the unit responsible for military honors funerals. His decorations include the Bronze Star Medal, the Combat Infantry Badge, and the Ranger Tab. After leaving active duty in 2009, Cotton ran for Congress in 2012, winning Arkansas's 4th Congressional District. After his term, he set his sights on the Senate, announcing his candidacy in August 2013 and going on to win a decisive victory in the 2014 general election, flipping the seat from Democratic to Republican. Cotton currently chairs the Senate Intelligence Committee, sits on the Armed Services Committee and the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources, and since November 2024 has served as Chairman of the Senate Republican Conference — the third-ranking position in Senate Republican leadership. Cotton has established himself as a leading figure within the Republican Party, with a particular focus on national security and conservative policy. Tom and his wife Anna have two sons, Gabriel and Daniel.

Senator Tom Cotton | | Tom Cotton is a sixth-generation Arkansan born and raised on his family's cattle farm in Yell County. He graduated from Dardanelle High School before earning a bachelor's degree from Harvard University and a J.D. from Harvard Law School. After clerking on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit and briefly practicing law, the September 11 attacks redirected the course of his life. Cotton joined the United States Army as an Infantry Officer and served nearly five years on active duty. He deployed to Iraq with the 101st Airborne Division and to Afghanistan with a Provincial Reconstruction Team. Between those combat tours, he led a platoon with The Old Guard at Arlington National Cemetery — the unit responsible for military honors funerals. His decorations include the Bronze Star Medal, the Combat Infantry Badge, and the Ranger Tab. After leaving active duty in 2009, Cotton ran for Congress in 2012, winning Arkansas's 4th Congressional District. After his term, he set his sights on the Senate, announcing his candidacy in August 2013 and going on to win a decisive victory in the 2014 general election, flipping the seat from Democratic to Republican.
